CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

Output format `path:line: <emoji> <severity>: <problem>. <fix>.` Use for "review this PR", "review my diff", "audit this file". Skips formatting nits unless they change meaning. (Tools: Read, Grep, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## railway
Railway MCP server. Manage your Railway projects, services, deployments, and more.

Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. - caveman:caveman-commit: Generate terse caveman-style commit message

- caveman:caveman-review: One-line code review comments
- caveman:caveman-stats: Real session token usage + lifetime savings + USD. Tweetable line via --share.
- caveman:caveman: Switch caveman intensity level (lite/full/ultra/wenyan)

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). ## Summary

There is **no general-purpose "preferred AI agent"** concept in the app yet. What exists is a narrower, issue-#49 feature: an **inline terminal-agent diagnosis** of failed shell commands, with an `AgentBackend` enum (claude | codex), a `terminalAgentBackend` preference string, and one already-working **headless `claude --print` invocation**. That invocation is exactly the seam you'd reuse to generate text programmatically.

---

## 1. The setting / preference

`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/DefaultsKeys.swift:66-84` — all agent keys live in one `extension Defaults.Keys` block:

```swift
static let terminalAgentAutoDiagnose = Key<Bool>("terminalAgentAutoDiagnose", default: false)
static let terminalAgentAutoDiagnosePrompted = Key<Bool>(
  "terminalAgentAutoDiagnosePrompted", default: false)
static let terminalAgentRedactSecrets = Key<Bool>("terminalAgentRedactSecrets", default: true)
/// Preferred agent backend: "auto" (claude, else codex), "claude", or "codex".
static let terminalAgentBackend = Key<String>("terminalAgentBackend", default: "auto")
static let terminalAgentModel = Key<String>(
  "terminalAgentModel", default: "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001")
```

Note the type: `terminalAgentBackend` is a **raw `String`** (`"auto" | "claude" | "codex"`), *not* the `AgentBackend` enum.

The enum of available agents — `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AgentRunner.swift:9-31`:

```swift
enum AgentBackend: String, Sendable, CaseIterable {
  case claude
  case codex
  var executable: String { rawValue }
  var supportsInlineDiagnosis: Bool { self == .claude }
  static func inlineBackend(installed: Set<AgentBackend>) -> AgentBackend?
  static func preferred(installed: Set<AgentBackend>) -> AgentBackend?
}
```

Settings UI: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/SettingsView.swift:357-391` (`private struct AgentSettingsPane`), with the picker tags hardcoded as `"auto"` / `"claude"` / `"codex"`. Pane registration: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/SettingsPane.swift` (`case agent`, label "Agent", symbol `sparkles`).

**Important gap:** `Defaults[.terminalAgentBackend]` is **write-only** — grep across app + tests finds reads only in `SettingsView.swift:358` (and for the caption text at :382). No runtime path consults it. Likewise `AgentBackend.preferred(installed:)` / `.inlineBackend(installed:)` are called **only from `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/AgentRunnerTests.swift:73-82`**, and nothing anywhere computes the `installed:` set (there is no agent-CLI detection code — contrast `ExternalEditor.installed` at `Core/ExternalEditor.swift:23`). Everything real hardcodes claude.

There is **no per-project / per-workroom agent override**. The only path-keyed Defaults maps are `runCommands` (`DefaultsKeys.swift:127`) and `workroomLabels` (`:178`).

---

## 2. How agents are launched today (interactive, in a ghostty surface)

Two call sites, both spawning a **run tab** whose PTY child is the command string:

- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:205-212` — builds a seeded command via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`, then `sessions.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)`.
- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:437-446` — `store.terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: "claude", cwd: cwd)` (bare, unseeded).

Command string construction — `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AgentPrompt.swift:56-61`:

```swift
static func investigateCommandLine(for state: AgentBannerState) -> String {
  let (failure, diagnosis) = state.failureAndDiagnosis
  let prompt = investigatePrompt(
    command: failure.command, exitCode: failure.exitCode, diagnosis: diagnosis)
  return "claude " + shellSingleQuoted(prompt)
}
static func shellSingleQuoted(_ s: String) -> String  // :87
```

So the "type" modelling the launched agent command is just a `String` — there is no `AgentInvocation`-style type on the interactive path (`AgentInvocation` at `AgentRunner.swift:34-37` is used only by the headless path).

Plumbing down to libghostty:
- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:573` `func addRunTab(for target: TerminalTarget, command: String, cwd: String, focus: Bool = true) -> TerminalTab`
- `:598` `func respawnRunTab(replacing oldID: TerminalTab.ID, for target: TerminalTarget, command: String, cwd: String, focus: Bool = true) -> TerminalTab`
- `:638` `private func makeRunTab(...)` → `:1117 makeTerminalTab(for:cwd:command:title:)` → `:214` `makeView` factory → `GhosttySurfaceView(workingDirectory: cwd, command: command)`
- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:156` `init(workingDirectory: String, command: String? = nil, spawnsSurface: Bool = true)`; `:236-243` sets `config.command = UnsafePointer(cmd)` + `config.wait_after_command = true`. libghostty runs the whole string through `sh -c`.
- For the *run-command* feature (not agents) there's a heavier wrapper: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1284` `private func runCommandLine(_ raw: String, pidPath: String) -> String` — wraps the command in a supervisor + login-interactive shell. Also relevant for injecting text into a live surface: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:813` `func sendText(_ string: String)` (used for "insert fix").

---

## 3. Existing non-interactive / headless agent invocation — YES

`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AgentRunner.swift:51-69`:

```swift
static func claudeInline(systemPrompt: String? = nil, model: String? = nil, prompt: String)
  -> AgentInvocation
{
  var arguments = [
    "--print",
    "--output-format", "json",
    "--permission-mode", "plan",
    "--allowed-tools", "none",
    "--no-session-persistence",
  ]
  if let model, !model.isEmpty { arguments.append(contentsOf: ["--model", model]) }
  if let systemPrompt, !systemPrompt.isEmpty {
    arguments.append(contentsOf: ["--system-prompt", systemPrompt])
  }
  arguments.append(prompt)
  return AgentInvocation(executable: AgentBackend.claude.executable, arguments: arguments)
}
```

The runner seam and default impl — `AgentRunner.swift:91-121`:

```swift
protocol AgentRunning: Sendable {
  func diagnoseInline(
    systemPrompt: String?, model: String?, prompt: String, cwd: String, timeout: TimeInterval
  ) async -> AgentRunOutcome
}

struct AgentRunner: AgentRunning {
  let executor: StatusCommandRunning
  init(executor: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner())
  func diagnoseInline(
    systemPrompt: String? = nil, model: String? = nil, prompt: String, cwd: String,
    timeout: TimeInterval = 60
  ) async -> AgentRunOutcome
  static func classify(_ result: CommandResult) -> AgentRunOutcome   // :125
  static func isAuthFailure(_ text: String) -> Bool                  // :140
}
```

Outcome type `enum AgentRunOutcome` at `:74-87` (`.success(stdout:)`, `.cliNotFound`, `.notAuthenticated`, `.timedOut`, `.emptyOutput`, `.failed(exitCode:stderr:)`).

Response parsing (reusable for text generation): `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AgentPrompt.swift:95` `static func parse(envelopeJSON: String) -> AgentDiagnosis?` — reads the `{"type":"result","is_error":false,"result":"…"}` envelope's `result` field; `:106 parseInner`, `:122 stripCodeFence`. For plain text generation you'd want just the envelope's `result`, which `parse` already extracts before handing it to the JSON-shape parser.

Orchestrator that owns debounce/cooldown/cancel/per-tab state: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:60-266` (`@MainActor final class`, injected `runner: AgentRunning`, `model: () -> String?` reading `Defaults[.terminalAgentModel]` at `:103-106`, `inlineCwd: String = NSTemporaryDirectory()` at `:114` — deliberately neutral so `CLAUDE.md` doesn't auto-load).

Test fake: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/UITestFixture.swift:743` `struct StubAgentRunner: AgentRunning`.

**No `codex exec` / codex headless invocation anywhere.** No agent CLI invocation of any kind in the Go CLI — `grep -rn "claude\|codex" --include="*.go" internal cmd main.go` yields only a comment in `cmd/add_project_create_test.go:253`.

---

## 4. The shell-out pattern from Swift (verbatim signatures)

The canonical process wrapper (hardened: concurrent stdout/stderr drain, timeout → SIGTERM → 2s → `killTree`, task-cancellation kill, 4 MB cap) — `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`:

- `:8-20` `struct CommandResult: Sendable, Equatable { let stdout: String; let stderr: String; let exitCode: Int32; let timedOut: Bool }` + `static let commandNotFound: Int32 = 127`, `static let gitFatal: Int32 = 128`, `var ok: Bool`
- `:24-27`
  ```swift
  protocol StatusCommandRunning: Sendable {
    func run(_ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String, timeout: TimeInterval)
      async -> CommandResult
  }
  ```
- `:39-44` `struct StatusCommandRunner: StatusCommandRunning, Sendable { var maxBytes: Int = 4 * 1024 * 1024; func run(_ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String, timeout: TimeInterval) async -> CommandResult }` — spawns via `/usr/bin/env` (`:46-47`) so the executable resolves on the augmented PATH; sets `env["PATH"] = ShellEnvironment.path()` at `:51`.

Other shell-out sites, all layered on the above or mirroring it:
- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/RustJJProvider.swift:232-234` — the jj CLI shell-out, `private static func run(_ exe: String, _ args: [String], cwd: URL, timeout: TimeInterval = 30) async throws -> String`, explicitly documented as routing through `StatusCommandRunner()` "rather than re-implementing it".
- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WorkroomCLI.swift:308-311` — `private func run(_ args: [String], timeout: TimeInterval, userInitiated: Bool = false, onEvent: ((StreamEvent) -> Void)? = nil) async throws -> CLIResult`, a separate hand-rolled `Process` for the bundled Go binary (NDJSON streaming on stderr).
- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ProcessTree.swift:29 childPids(of:)`, `:47 static func killTree(_ pid: pid_t)`.
- Async helpers `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/Timeout.swift`:
  - `:21` `func withTimeout<T: Sendable>(seconds: TimeInterval, _ operation: @escaping @Sendable () async throws -> T) async throws -> T`
  - `:65` `func runBlocking<T: Sendable>(qos: DispatchQoS.QoSClass = .userInitiated, _ work: @escaping @Sendable () throws -> T) async throws -> T` — for synchronous blocking work; keeps it off the fixed-width cooperative pool.
- Quoting: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/CommandLineInstaller.swift:133` `static func shellQuoted(_ s: String) -> String` (and the duplicate `AgentPrompt.shellSingleQuoted` at `AgentPrompt.swift:87`).

**For a new headless agent call, use `StatusCommandRunning.run(_:_:in:timeout:)` (via a small `AgentRunning`-style seam), not a raw `Process`.**

---

## 5. Child-process environment (floor + probe)

`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ShellEnvironment.swift` — `enum ShellEnvironment` (`:26`). Public API:

| Line | Signature | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `:285` | `static func path() -> String` | **PATH only.** For unattended/automatic work (status sweep, VCS reads). What `StatusCommandRunner` uses. |
| `:292` | `static func environment() -> [String: String]` | **Full env dict for a spawned process.** For user-initiated work whose child is the user's own code (setup/teardown scripts). Falls back to `ProcessInfo` env + `floorPath()` + `appOverrides` before the first probe. |
| `:309` | `@discardableResult static func refresh(shell: String = loginShell()) async -> [String: String]` | Re-probe the user's login+interactive shell; single-flighted, generation-guarded, never clears a good cache. Call before spawning if a tool may have just been installed. |
| `:84` | `static func floorPath(etcPaths: String = "/etc/paths", etcPathsD: String = "/etc/paths.d", inherited: String? = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["PATH"]) -> String` | The no-subprocess PATH floor (`/etc/paths` + `/etc/paths.d/*` + `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin` — `:71-76`, explicitly listed for the `claude` installer, issue #49). |
| `:32` / `:43` | `static func loginShell() -> String` / `static func loginShellExecutable(shell: String = loginShell()) -> String` | |
| `:53` | `static func loginShellInvocation(script: String, shell: String = loginShell()) -> (argv: (executable: String, args: [String]), commandString: String)` | Two forms: `argv` for `Process`, `commandString` for libghostty's `config.command`. |
| `:176` | `static func probe(shell: String = loginShell(), timeout: TimeInterval = 3) -> Result<[String: String], ProbeFailure>` | Blocking — must go through `runBlocking`. |
| `:264` | `static func merge(probed: [String: String], floor: String = floorPath()) -> [String: String]` | |
| `:349` | `static func resetForTesting()` | |

`appOverrides` (`:146-149`) force `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` / `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` last so no dotfile can revoke them. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once in `WorkroomApp.init`.

Pattern for the two callers: `WorkroomCLI.run` picks `ShellEnvironment.environment()` when `userInitiated` else `ProcessInfo` env + `ShellEnvironment.path()` (`WorkroomCLI.swift:319-323`); `WorkroomCLI.create`/`delete` `await ShellEnvironment.refresh()` first (`:183`, `:200`, `:237`).

1. Add a builder alongside `AgentInvocationBuilder.claudeInline` (`AgentRunner.swift:40-70`) — e.g. `claudeGenerate(systemPrompt:model:prompt:)` using `--print --output-format json --allowed-tools none --no-session-persistence` (keep `--permission-mode plan` if you want the no-tools guarantee).
2. Run it through `StatusCommandRunning.run(exe, args, in: cwd, timeout:)` (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:42`) — you get the `/usr/bin/env` PATH resolution, timeout, `killTree`, cancellation and output cap for free. Reuse `AgentRunner.classify` (`:125`) for the outcome mapping.
3. Extract the text with `AgentPrompt.parse(envelopeJSON:)`'s envelope step (`AgentPrompt.swift:95-101`) — you likely want just the `result` string, not `parseInner`'s diagnosis-shaped JSON.
4. Pass `cwd: NSTemporaryDirectory()` if you don't want `CLAUDE.md` auto-loaded (the pattern `TerminalAgentManager.inlineCwd` uses, `:114`), or the workroom path if you do.
5. To honour the preference, you must **add the missing read** of `Defaults[.terminalAgentBackend]` plus an installed-agent detection (nothing exists; `AgentBackend.preferred(installed:)` is ready but uncalled). Note codex has no zero-tools mode (documented at `AgentRunner.swift:7-8`), so a codex text-generation path needs its own argv (`codex exec …`) which does not exist anywhere yet.
6. Redaction, if input includes captured output: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/SecretRedactor.swift:35` `static func redact(_ text: String) -> String`.

| Line | Signature | Use |
|---|---|---|

## Practical path to "invoke an agent to generate text"

1. Add a builder alongside `AgentInvocationBuilder.claudeInline` (`AgentRunner.swift:40-70`) — e.g. `claudeGenerate(systemPrompt:model:prompt:)` using `--print --output-format json --allowed-tools none --no-session-persistence` (keep `--permission-mode plan` if you want the no-tools guarantee).
2. Run it through `StatusCommandRunning.run(exe, args, in: cwd, timeout:)` (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:42`) — you get the `/usr/bin/env` PATH resolution, timeout, `killTree`, cancellation and output cap for free. Reuse `AgentRunner.classify` (`:125`) for the outcome mapping.
3. Extract the text with `AgentPrompt.parse(envelopeJSON:)`'s envelope step (`AgentPrompt.swift:95-101`) — you likely want just the `result` string, not `parseInner`'s diagnosis-shaped JSON.
4. Pass `cwd: NSTemporaryDirectory()` if you don't want `CLAUDE.md` auto-loaded (the pattern `TerminalAgentManager.inlineCwd` uses, `:114`), or the workroom path if you do.
5. To honour the preference, you must **add the missing read** of `Defaults[.terminalAgentBackend]` plus an installed-agent detection (nothing exists; `AgentBackend.preferred(installed:)` is ready but uncalled). Note codex has no zero-tools mode (documented at `AgentRunner.swift:7-8`), so a codex text-generation path needs its own argv (`codex exec …`) which does not exist anywhere yet.
6. Redaction, if input includes captured output: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/SecretRedactor.swift:35` `static func redact(_ text: String) -> String`.

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Which agent CLI backs a diagnosis (issue #49). Capabilities differ per decision X1:
4	/// - `.claude` can run a **true no-tools** inline diagnosis (`--allowed-tools none --permission-mode
5	///   plan`, verified: returns a JSON envelope with no tool calls), so it backs the inline/automatic
6	///   path AND the Investigate hand-off.
7	/// - `.codex exec` has no zero-tools mode (`-s read-only` still runs read-only commands), so it is
8	///   **Investigate-only** — never the silent inline path. (Investigate is wired in the banner, T8.)
9	enum AgentBackend: String, Sendable, CaseIterable {
10	  case claude
11	  case codex
12	
13	  /// The executable name, resolved on the augmented PATH by `StatusCommandRunner` via `/usr/bin/env`.
14	  var executable: String { rawValue }
15	
16	  /// Only claude can run the inline diagnosis with no tool execution (X1).
17	  var supportsInlineDiagnosis: Bool { self == .claude }
18	
19	  /// The inline-diagnosis backend among those installed: claude or nothing (X1). When nil, the UI
20	  /// offers Investigate-with-codex only rather than a silent inline run.
21	  static func inlineBackend(installed: Set<AgentBackend>) -> AgentBackend? {
22	    installed.contains(.claude) ? .claude : nil
23	  }
24	
25	  /// Preferred backend for the Investigate hand-off: claude, else codex.
26	  static func preferred(installed: Set<AgentBackend>) -> AgentBackend? {
27	    if installed.contains(.claude) { return .claude }
28	    if installed.contains(.codex) { return .codex }
29	    return nil
30	  }
31	}
32	
33	/// A resolved CLI command: the executable plus its argv (the prompt is the trailing positional).
34	struct AgentInvocation: Equatable, Sendable {
35	  let executable: String
36	  let arguments: [String]
37	}
38	
39	/// Pure argv construction (unit-tested; no process spawning).
40	enum AgentInvocationBuilder {
41	  /// The inline, no-tools claude diagnosis (issue #49, X1). Verified against the installed claude:
42	  /// - `--print --output-format json` → a single JSON result envelope (the `result` field is the
43	  ///   text; parsed in T5),
44	  /// - `--permission-mode plan` + `--allowed-tools none` → no edits, no execution, no tool calls
45	  ///   (the allowlist is exclusive, so the bogus name denies every real tool),
46	  /// - `--no-session-persistence` → the prompt/output don't land in claude's session history.
47	  /// The working directory is supplied to the executor (`run(in:)`), not as a claude flag.
48	  /// `systemPrompt`, when given, replaces claude's heavy default system prompt — it both shapes the
49	  /// output and cuts token cost (task #15). `model`, when given, pins a cheap/fast model so the
50	  /// diagnosis doesn't run on the user's (often Opus) default. The prompt stays the trailing positional.
51	  static func claudeInline(systemPrompt: String? = nil, model: String? = nil, prompt: String)
52	    -> AgentInvocation
53	  {
54	    var arguments = [
55	      "--print",
56	      "--output-format", "json",
57	      "--permission-mode", "plan",
58	      "--allowed-tools", "none",
59	      "--no-session-persistence",
60	    ]
61	    if let model, !model.isEmpty {
62	      arguments.append(contentsOf: ["--model", model])
63	    }
64	    if let systemPrompt, !systemPrompt.isEmpty {
65	      arguments.append(contentsOf: ["--system-prompt", systemPrompt])
66	    }
67	    arguments.append(prompt)
68	    return AgentInvocation(executable: AgentBackend.claude.executable, arguments: arguments)
69	  }
70	}
71	
72	/// The raw outcome of an inline diagnosis run, before the model's text is parsed into an
73	/// `AgentDiagnosis` (T5). Distinct cases so the banner can show actionable states (X1/A2).
74	enum AgentRunOutcome: Sendable, Equatable {
75	  /// Process succeeded; `stdout` is the raw JSON envelope (claude `--output-format json`).
76	  case success(stdout: String)
77	  /// `/usr/bin/env` exit 127 — the agent CLI isn't on PATH.
78	  case cliNotFound
79	  /// Non-zero exit whose output looks like an auth/login failure.
80	  case notAuthenticated
81	  /// The timeout fired.
82	  case timedOut
83	  /// Succeeded but produced no usable text.
84	  case emptyOutput
85	  /// Any other non-zero exit (stderr tail kept for the banner / logs).
86	  case failed(exitCode: Int32, stderr: String)
87	}
88	
89	/// A seam (mirrors `StatusCommandRunning`) so the inline-agent manager (T6) is unit-testable with a
90	/// fake runner — no real `claude`/`codex` process.
91	protocol AgentRunning: Sendable {
92	  /// Run an inline, no-tools diagnosis (claude only, X1). `systemPrompt` replaces claude's default
93	  /// to shape output + cut cost; `model` pins a cheap/fast model (task #15). `cwd` is where claude
94	  /// runs — callers should pass a NEUTRAL dir (not the project) so `CLAUDE.md` doesn't auto-load:
95	  /// the inline path has no tools and gets all context from `prompt`, so the real failure cwd
96	  /// belongs in the prompt text, not here.
97	  func diagnoseInline(
98	    systemPrompt: String?, model: String?, prompt: String, cwd: String, timeout: TimeInterval
99	  ) async -> AgentRunOutcome
100	}
101	
102	/// Default `AgentRunning`: builds the claude inline argv and runs it through the existing
103	/// `StatusCommandRunning` executor (CQ1 — no duplicated process/drain/timeout/cancel code). The
104	/// executor's process-group termination (X2, T3) reaps any agent child processes on cancel/timeout.
105	struct AgentRunner: AgentRunning {
106	  let executor: StatusCommandRunning
107	
108	  init(executor: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner()) {
109	    self.executor = executor
110	  }
111	
112	  func diagnoseInline(
113	    systemPrompt: String? = nil, model: String? = nil, prompt: String, cwd: String,
114	    timeout: TimeInterval = 60
115	  ) async -> AgentRunOutcome {
116	    let invocation = AgentInvocationBuilder.claudeInline(
117	      systemPrompt: systemPrompt, model: model, prompt: prompt)
118	    let result = await executor.run(
119	      invocation.executable, invocation.arguments, in: cwd, timeout: timeout)
120	    return Self.classify(result)
121	  }
122	
123	  /// Map a raw process result to a diagnosis outcome. Pure + unit-tested. stdout carries the model's
124	  /// JSON; stderr is treated only as diagnostics (CLI warnings must not be mistaken for the result).
125	  static func classify(_ result: CommandResult) -> AgentRunOutcome {
126	    if result.timedOut { return .timedOut }
127	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .cliNotFound }
128	    if result.exitCode != 0 {
129	      if isAuthFailure(result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout) {
130	        return .notAuthenticated
131	      }
132	      return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, stderr: String(result.stderr.suffix(2000)))
133	    }
134	    return result.stdout.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
135	      ? .emptyOutput
136	      : .success(stdout: result.stdout)
137	  }

139	  /// Heuristic auth/login-failure detection over the agent CLI's combined output.
140	  static func isAuthFailure(_ text: String) -> Bool {
141	    let lowered = text.lowercased()
142	    return [
143	      "not authenticated", "unauthorized", "authentication", "invalid api key", "invalid_api_key",
144	      "please log in", "please login", "run `claude login`", "run claude login", "no api key",
145	    ].contains { lowered.contains($0) }
146	  }

# macapp/CLAUDE.md

The Workroom macOS app: a SwiftUI (macOS 15+) front-end that bundles the `workroom`
Go binary and drives it over the CLI's `--json` contract. See README.md for full
architecture, signing, and notarization detail — this file is the quick reference.

## Dev tasks (Makefile)

Every dev task runs through the **repo-root `Makefile`**, namespaced `app-*` (run from the repo
root, not `macapp/`):

```bash
make app-run        # canonical local loop: xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug) → relaunch
make app-build      # xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug)
make app-test       # xcodebuild test (WorkroomAppTests) — parallel; APP_TEST_FLAGS= to serialize
make app-generate   # force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
make app-vcs        # build the Rust VCS core → WrVcs SwiftPM package (auto-run before app builds)
make app-format     # swift-format, rewrite sources in place
make app-lint       # swift-format --strict (non-zero on any violation — the hard gate)
make app-release    # Release build → notarize → staple → DMG installer (Scripts/release.sh)
make app-icon       # regenerate AppIcon PNGs (Scripts/make-icon.swift)
make app-clean      # remove DerivedData + .xcodeproj
```

Builds reuse `macapp/DerivedData/` so the Swift packages (incl. the GhosttyKit xcframework)
aren't re-resolved/re-downloaded every build. (`cli-*` targets cover the Go CLI — see the root
CLAUDE.md.)

## VCS core (Rust jj + SwiftGitX git)

Workroom reads VCS data through **two backends behind one Swift layer** (the app is growing into a
VCS-first IDE — issue #59 is the first brick):

- **jj → Rust `jj-lib` via UniFFI.** The `vcs/` Rust workspace (jj-only) builds a static xcframework
  + generated Swift into the local SwiftPM package `vcs/swift/WrVcs` — the app does `import WrVcs`.
- **git → SwiftGitX (libgit2), pure Swift.** git has a mature native Swift path; jj has none — so
  only jj needs the Rust/UniFFI bridge. (An all-Rust core with gix was tried and dropped: gix bought
  no real unification and libgit2 is the more complete git engine.)

**Three reads reach past SwiftGitX**, all linking the `libgit2` C API **directly** (its own SPM package
in `project.yml`, URL + version identical to SwiftGitX's own dependency so SwiftPM sees one package
identity). `Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init` and hands out raw `git_repository`
handles (SwiftGitX inits inside `Repository.open`, which a direct C caller can't rely on); these four
files are the only ones in the app touching raw libgit2:

- **Push state — `Core/GitGraph.swift`.** SwiftGitX cannot express a commit *range*: its
  `CommitSequence` only calls `git_revwalk_push`, never `git_revwalk_hide`, it exposes no
  merge-base/graph helper, and its repository pointer is `internal` — so "which commits aren't on
  `origin` yet" (`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*`) needs the C API. The jj side answers the same
  question natively with one `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)` revset. Push state is
  **origin-scoped** and any unreadable ref degrades the WHOLE page to "unknown" (no badge) rather than
  a partial answer.
- **Commit diffs — `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`.** Rename detection is `git_diff_find_similar` run over a
  live `git_diff`, and a SwiftGitX `Diff` materializes its deltas/patches in an `internal` init and
  frees the `git_diff` before returning, so there's nothing left to detect on. Without it a committed
  rename read as delete + add while `git show` showed one rename row (git defaults to
  `diff.renames=true`), and a root commit's diff came back empty (SwiftGitX diffs it against itself).
  Detection options are NULL, which is what makes libgit2 read the repo's own `diff.renames` /
  `diff.renamelimit` — naming a flag explicitly suppresses that config read, so a repo set to
  `diff.renames=false` or `=copies` would silently disagree with its own CLI. Typechanges are included
  (`GIT_DIFF_INCLUDE_TYPECHANGE`); without it libgit2 splits a file↔symlink change into delete + add
  on the SAME path, giving the file list two rows with one `id`. `GitProvider.changeset`/`.fileDiff`
  both read through it, so the History file list and the patch text can't disagree.
- **Working-tree ± line counts — `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`**, via `git_diff_get_stats`. SwiftGitX
  surfaces no diffstat, and its `Diff` is **eager**: `Diff.init` builds a `Patch` per delta and
  materializes every hunk line into a Swift `String` before the caller sees it. Summing those for the
  badge cost one `String` per changed line of the whole worktree on **every** status refresh, so the
  counts moved to libgit2, which counts in C and allocates nothing Swift-side. The diff itself is
  irreducible — that's what `git diff --shortstat` costs too. With `changeset` now counting through
  `GitCommitDiff`, **no** `+N −M` in the app is summed off SwiftGitX hunk lines any more, which also
  ends a real bug: that sum counted the EOFNL markers (`\ No newline at end of file`) as lines, so
  changing only a file's trailing newline reported two deletions where git reports `1 insertion(+),
  1 deletion(-)`. libgit2 skips them, as `git diff --shortstat`/`--numstat` do. It runs
  `git_diff_find_similar` too, for the same reason `GitCommitDiff` does: the file list beside these
  counts already pairs renames (libgit2 status' `.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so without it
  a staged rename rendered as one "renamed" row badged `+N −N` while `git diff HEAD --shortstat`
  reported `0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

**Read surface & routing.** `Core/VCSProviding.swift` is the one Swift protocol; `VCS.provider(for:)`
routes by repo kind. `RustJJProvider` maps `WrVcs.*` → app-native models, `GitProvider` wraps
SwiftGitX. `WorkroomStatusResolver` and `BranchResolver` read through this layer — **the jj CLI
parsers are gone** (log/changeset/currentRef/workingStatus are all native jj-lib).

**The one mutating read: `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`.** jj's working copy is itself a commit, so
on-disk edits don't exist to jj-lib until snapshotted — a working-copy status read therefore *must*
snapshot `@` first: it takes the working-copy lock and rewrites `@` (modeled on jayjay's
`refresh_working_copy`). Everything else (log/changeset/currentRef) is a read-only `load_at_head`
with no lock. Because it mutates, **only test snapshot changes on throwaway repos** (corruption
risk). Line counts come from the SAME native read — `changed_files` materializes each changed file's
two sides and counts them, so `resolveJJ` fires no `jj diff --stat` process (it used to; see
`40456bae`). Oversized and binary files report no count rather than being read whole. Cargo coverage:
`vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/working_status.rs` + `line_stats.rs`; Swift coverage:
`WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.testJJ*`.

`make app-vcs` (→ `vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh`) builds the Rust artifacts and **runs automatically
before `app-build`/`app-test`/`app-generate`** (a Makefile prerequisite). Requirements:

- **`protoc`** on PATH (`brew install protobuf`) — a build-time dep of jj-lib.
- arm64 by default; **`make app-release` builds universal** (`VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal`), which
  needs **rustup `stable` ≥ 1.93** + `rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (Homebrew's rust can't cross-compile; the script preflights this and errors clearly).
- **Unchanged inputs are a no-op.** The script hashes the Rust sources, manifests/lockfile, itself,
  `rustc --version` and the arch flavour into `vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks/.build-stamp`, and exits
  early when that matches and the outputs exist. `WR_VCS_FORCE=1 make app-vcs` rebuilds regardless.
  CI leans on this: it caches the *outputs* keyed on the same inputs, so a commit that doesn't touch
  `vcs/` skips the ~4-minute crate-graph build (and `make app-test`'s own `app-vcs` prerequisite
  stays free).
- **Xcode-driven builds are gated, not auto-fixed.** ⌘R/⌘U (and a raw `xcodebuild`) skip the
  Makefile, so they'd otherwise link the last-built core. A `Rust VCS core up to date` pre-build
  phase runs `build-apple.sh --check` and **fails the build** with `run 'make app-vcs'` when the
  stamp doesn't match `vcs/`. It can't rebuild for you: SPM extracts the binaryTarget's xcframework
  before target build phases run, so a fresh `.a` wouldn't reach that build's link. Silently linking
  a stale core cost a debugging session once — conflicted files read as `.modified` because the
  linked core predated a merged per-file-conflict fix.

The xcframework + generated Swift are **gitignored and regenerated**; only `Package.swift` + a
`shim.c` are tracked. Packaging note: the xcframework is **library-only** (no headers) and the FFI
Clang module (`wr_vcs_uniffiFFI`) is a separate SPM C target — a headers-bearing static xcframework
copies its `module.modulemap` into the shared `Debug/include/` and collides with GhosttyKit's
("Multiple commands produce include/module.modulemap").

## Formatting & linting

Swift is formatted/linted with **swift-format** (bundled with the Xcode toolchain — run via
`xcrun swift-format`, no install). Config `macapp/.swift-format` (2-space, 100 cols) covers
`WorkroomApp/` + `WorkroomAppTests/` only (not the `Scripts/*.swift` tools). Use `make app-format`
/ `make app-lint`. Every Xcode/`xcodebuild` build also runs a `swift-format lint` pre-build phase
that surfaces violations as **warnings** (non-fatal — `make app-lint` is the hard gate). Run
`make app-format` before committing.

## Gotchas

- **The Swift module is `Workroom`** (the target is `WorkroomApp`; `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` is pinned
  to `Workroom` in `project.yml`). Tests use `@testable import Workroom`. The pin matters because
  `PRODUCT_NAME` is **per-config**: `Workroom` for Release, `Workroom Dev` for Debug (see below) —
  without the pin the Debug module would become `Workroom_Dev` and break the import. A test
  target's `TEST_HOST` must point at the Debug product (`Workroom Dev.app/Contents/MacOS/Workroom
  Dev`); XcodeGen's auto-derived (target-name-based) host is wrong and fails with "Could not find
  test host".
- **Debug builds run side by side with the release build.** The Debug config has a distinct
  identity — bundle id `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, product/display name `Workroom Dev`,
  and the amber `AppIcon-Dev` icon set — so a local build doesn't fight the installed release
  `Workroom` for activation, the key window, preferences (separate UserDefaults domain via the
  bundle id), or the system-wide ⌘§ hotkey. The Debug build deliberately **doesn't register ⌘§**
  and **doesn't run Sparkle scheduled checks** (`#if DEBUG` in `WorkroomApp.swift` / `Updater.swift`)
  so it can't grab the global hotkey or try to "update" itself to the release DMG. Both builds
  still share the CLI config at `~/.config/workroom/config.json` (the bundled CLI has no
  config-path override), so they show the same projects/workrooms. `make app-run` only kills the
  `Workroom Dev` instance, never your release build. The two app icons (`make app-icon` renders
  both) are identical except for the tile gradient.
- **Adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file needs an `xcodegen generate`.** XcodeGen
  expands the source glob into explicit file refs in the (gitignored) `.xcodeproj`, so
  the change is invisible (or, for a deleted/renamed file, a hard "Build input file
  cannot be found" error) until the project is regenerated. The `make app-*` build
  targets now run `xcodegen generate` every time, so this is handled automatically —
  it only bites when building from Xcode directly (regenerate, or run `make app-generate`).
- **SourceKit "Cannot find type X in scope" is usually noise.** The single-file indexer
  doesn't see sibling files; a clean `xcodebuild` is authoritative.
- **The terminal is libghostty** (`libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework, pinned
  `exactVersion: 1.2.3` in project.yml). The embedding C API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT —
  don't float it. The terminal surface (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`) + runtime
  (`GhosttyApp`/`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`) are ours; the bundled `Resources/ghostty` (terminfo +
  shell-integration) must ship for the engine to start. Pre-GA, the plan is to move to a
  self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork.
- **The child environment has two layers, and only one of them is reliable** (`Core/ShellEnvironment.swift`).
  A Finder-launched `.app` gets a minimal PATH, so: the **floor** (`floorPath()`) reads `/etc/paths`
  + `/etc/paths.d/*` — `path_helper`'s own inputs — with no shell at all, and that alone resolves
  Postgres.app's `psql`; the **probe** (`refresh()`) then runs one `$SHELL -ilc` for what only an
  interactive login shell knows (`.zshrc` PATH entries, mise shims). The probe is best-effort by
  design: its failures degrade to the floor, so a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux` costs enrichment
  and never the bug. Three traps worth knowing: **`path_helper` APPENDS** the PATH it's handed, so
  the probe must be spawned with a *cleared* `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` or Homebrew ends
  up at the tail; the payload is a **raw `env -0` stream between UUID markers** because command
  substitution strips NULs and the user's `base64` may be GNU's (wraps at 76 cols); and the deadline
  is a `DispatchWorkItem` **inside** the blocking closure, because `withTimeout` cannot cancel a
  `runBlocking` call and would leak a shell per invocation. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once,
  in `WorkroomApp.init` — a later write would race the status sweep's `ProcessInfo.environment`
  reads. Everything else reads `ShellEnvironment.path()` (PATH only, for the automatic sweep) or
  `.environment()` (the full environment, for setup/teardown scripts).
- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.

## Layout

**VCS info that only the GUI needs** (e.g. the sidebar root row's current branch/bookmark)
is resolved app-side in `Core/BranchResolver.swift` (per project, async, with a per-call
timeout) — deliberately NOT added to the `workroom --json` contract, which the human CLI
never shows.

`WorkroomApp/Core/` — store, CLI wrapper, terminal sessions, models, theme.
`WorkroomApp/Views/` — `NavigationSplitView` tree sidebar + terminal detail.
`Scripts/` — `run.sh` (local), `build-helper.sh` (embeds+signs the Go binary), `release.sh`
(build → notarize → staple → DMG → EdDSA-sign for Sparkle), `appcast.sh` (publishes the Sparkle
appcast to the fixed `appcast` release), `appcast-notes.sh` (re-renders a published item's
`<description>` from the current release body — see "Auto-update" below), `make-icon.swift`
(regenerates the `AppIcon` PNGs in `Assets.xcassets` — run `swift Scripts/make-icon.swift`).

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

`Core/Updater.swift` wraps Sparkle's `SPUStandardUpdaterController` (the "Check for Updates…"
menu item + the Settings toggle bind to it). The `SU*` keys in `project.yml` (`SUFeedURL`,
`SUPublicEDKey`, `SUEnableAutomaticChecks`) configure it. **Versioning is tag-driven** —
`CFBundleShortVersionString`/`CFBundleVersion` resolve from `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`/
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, which `release.sh` injects from the git tag (build number =
commit count, so it only ever increases — Sparkle compares it). The appcast feed is an asset
on the fixed `appcast` GitHub release. See `README.md` ("Auto-update") for the one-time keypair
setup and the `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.

**Release channels (issue #91) — two build identities.** The **main** app (`Release` config)
switches `stable`⟷`pre` at runtime via the *Settings ▸ General ▸ Release channel* picker
(`ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` = stable/pre only). **Workroom Nightly** is a separate side-by-side
product — the `Nightly` build config in `project.yml` (bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, name, violet
`AppIcon-Nightly`, `WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL=nightly` → the `WorkroomReleaseChannel` Info.plist
marker read by `ReleaseChannel.current`/`isNightlyBuild`), extending the Debug/"Workroom Dev"
per-config identity pattern to a third identity.

`Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` returns `{nightly}` on the nightly build and the picked stable/pre
floor otherwise; one appcast feed carries all channels (`Scripts/appcast.sh` tags items via the
shared `Scripts/channel-helper.sh`; stable stays untagged = Sparkle default), and Sparkle's
bundle-id check stops either identity installing the other's DMG. Nightly is a single **rolling**
item; appcast idempotency keys on `(channel, build)`. `build-helper.sh` bakes both
`-X main.version=$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and `-X main.channel=$(WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL)` into the
bundled CLI, and `CommandLineInstaller` symlinks it as `workroom` (main) or `workroom-nightly`
(nightly build) so both coexist in PATH. `Updater.migrateReleaseChannelIfNeeded` opts an upgrading
beta user into `pre` and coerces a legacy `.nightly` selection to `.stable` (main build only).

**Release-notes in the update dialog.** Sparkle's dialog renders the appcast item's
`<description>`. `appcast.sh` (run during the release) embeds the GitHub release body as that
description — but at release time the body is still goreleaser's raw commit list, since the
curated notes are written afterwards. So a second path keeps them in sync: the
`.github/workflows/appcast-notes.yml` workflow fires on every `release: edited` event and runs
`Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`, which re-renders the matching item's `<description>` from the
release's *current* body. Curating a release's notes therefore auto-refreshes what the update
dialog shows; no rebuild needed. To fix an already-published feed by hand, run it directly:
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) macapp/Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

questions.question: How should the git Commit actually write? (SwiftGitX can stage adds + commit in-process, but its public API cannot stage DELETIONS, and libgit2 runs no hooks and won't GPG-sign)

options.label: `git` CLI (Recommended)
options.description: `git add -A` + `git commit -m` via the existing StatusCommandRunner (the app already shells `git` for rev-parse and ls-files). Gets deletions, pre-commit hooks, commit.gpgsign, commit.template and user.name/email exactly as the user's terminal does. Symmetric with the jj side, which must shell out anyway.

options.label: SwiftGitX + raw libgit2
options.description: In-process `repo.add(paths:)` + `repo.commit(message:)`, plus raw `git_index_remove_bypath` for deletions. Stays native like the read layer, but silently skips pre-commit hooks and produces unsigned commits even when `commit.gpgsign=true`.

questions.question: Where does the commit box sit in the Changes section?

options.label: Top, under the header
options.description: Between the branch/bookmark header divider and the changed-file list. Scrolls with the content. Simplest — the pane is an intrinsic-height NSScrollView today.

options.label: Bottom, pinned
options.description: File list scrolls above, commit box fixed at the bottom of the section — the Tower/Fork/GitHub Desktop convention. Needs the pane's `fill` layout mode instead of intrinsic height.

4	/// The right inspector composed as a raw `NSSplitView` (horizontal dividers, panes stacked top to
5	/// bottom) instead of a SwiftUI `VStack`. Each section is one arranged subview: a **sticky header +
6	/// scrollable body** — the section header is a fixed `NSHostingController` at the top, the body
7	/// lives in a native `NSScrollView` below it, so a section scrolls its content when cramped (or
8	/// dragged small) without ever scrolling its own disclosure header out of view.
9	///
10	/// Sizing: the default distribution is **equal** among expanded panes (collapsed panes pinned to
11	/// the header), realised once via `setPosition(ofDividerAt:)`; thereafter the user drags dividers
12	/// freely (raw `NSSplitView` gives native drag + proportional window-resize) and a per-pane height
13	/// constraint enforces the floor / the collapsed pin.
14	///
15	/// Why a **raw** `NSSplitView` and not `NSSplitViewController`: the controller's `adjustSubviews`
16	/// hugs every pane to its content's fitting size and dumps the slack on the lowest-holding-priority
17	/// pane, overriding `setPosition` on every layout pass — so equal sizing is impossible there. A raw
18	/// split view only positions dividers and respects per-subview Auto Layout constraints; it never
19	/// hugs content. Why AppKit at all (vs the old SwiftUI `VStack`): it kills the header-title "swim"
20	/// (each header is its own stable hosting view; collapse moves *sibling* panes, not a per-frame
21	/// SwiftUI re-layout of a translating `Text`) and gives free system-preference auto-hiding scrollers
22	/// (a raw `NSScrollView` tracks "Show scroll bars").
23	
24	// MARK: - Pane: sticky header + scrollable body
25	
26	/// One split pane. The section header is a fixed-height `NSHostingController` pinned to the top; the
27	/// body sits below it in one of two hosting modes:
28	///
29	/// - **scroll** (default): the body is an `NSHostingController` (`.intrinsicContentSize`) inside a
30	///   vertically-scrolling `NSScrollView` — it reports its natural height and the AppKit scroll view
31	///   scrolls when the pane is shorter than the content (auto-hiding scrollers, tracks the system
32	///   "Show scroll bars" preference).
33	/// - **fill** (`fillsBody`): the body hosting view instead FILLS the pane below the header and is
34	///   expected to scroll ITSELF (a SwiftUI `ScrollView`). This bypasses the `.intrinsicContentSize` →
35	///   `NSScrollView` bridge, so an inline height animation inside the body (the History pane's
36	///   divergence expander) is driven entirely by SwiftUI and can't fight AppKit's scroll-container
37	///   resize-anchoring — the source of the visible content shift the bridge produced.
38	///
39	/// When collapsed, the body is hidden and the enclosing split pins the pane to the header height.
40	final class InspectorPaneViewController: NSViewController {
41	  private let headerHost = NSHostingController(rootView: AnyView(EmptyView()))
42	  private let bodyScroll = NSScrollView()
43	  private let bodyHost = NSHostingController(rootView: AnyView(EmptyView()))
44	  /// Whether the body fills the pane and scrolls itself (vs. the default `NSScrollView` hosting).
45	  /// Must be set before the view first loads.
46	  var fillsBody = false
47	
48	  override func loadView() {
49	    let container = NSView()
50	
51	    headerHost.view.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
52	    let bodyView: NSView
53	
54	    if fillsBody {
55	      // Fill mode: the body hosting view fills below the header and owns its own scrolling.
56	      bodyHost.sizingOptions = []
57	      addChild(bodyHost)
58	      bodyView = bodyHost.view
59	      bodyView.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
60	      container.addSubview(bodyView)
61	    } else {
62	      // Scroll mode: the body scroll view is added FIRST, then the header, so the header is topmost
63	      // in z-order — the opaque sticky header always sits above the scrolling body so content can
64	      // never bleed over the title during a resize.
65	      bodyHost.sizingOptions = [.intrinsicContentSize]
66	      addChild(bodyHost)
67	      let document = bodyHost.view
68	      document.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
69	      bodyScroll.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
70	      bodyScroll.hasVerticalScroller = true
71	      bodyScroll.hasHorizontalScroller = false
72	      bodyScroll.autohidesScrollers = true
73	      bodyScroll.drawsBackground = false
74	      bodyScroll.documentView = document
75	      container.addSubview(bodyScroll)
76	      bodyView = bodyScroll
77	      NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
78	        // Document pinned to the clip view's top/width (free height → it grows to content and the
79	        // scroll view scrolls when the pane is shorter than the content).
80	        document.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bodyScroll.contentView.topAnchor),
81	        document.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bodyScroll.contentView.leadingAnchor),
82	        document.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bodyScroll.contentView.trailingAnchor),
83	        document.widthAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bodyScroll.contentView.widthAnchor),
84	      ])
85	    }
86	
87	    addChild(headerHost)
88	    container.addSubview(headerHost.view)
89	
90	    NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
91	      // Sticky header: fixed height at the top.
92	      headerHost.view.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.topAnchor),
93	      headerHost.view.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.leadingAnchor),
94	      headerHost.view.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.trailingAnchor),
95	      headerHost.view.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorPanePolicy.headerHeight),
96	
97	      // Body fills the rest of the pane below the header.
98	      bodyView.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: headerHost.view.bottomAnchor),
99	      bodyView.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.leadingAnchor),
100	      bodyView.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.trailingAnchor),
101	      bodyView.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: container.bottomAnchor),
102	    ])
103	    view = container
104	  }

106	  /// Swap the hosted header + body. The body is hidden when collapsed so only the header shows (the
107	  /// enclosing split also pins a collapsed pane to the header height).
108	  func setContent(header: AnyView, body: AnyView, collapsed: Bool) {
109	    _ = view  // ensure loaded
110	    headerHost.rootView = header
111	    bodyHost.rootView = body
112	    (fillsBody ? bodyHost.view : bodyScroll).isHidden = collapsed

118	/// Owns the raw `NSSplitView` and the three pane child controllers. Sizing rules:
119	///
120	/// - A per-pane height constraint (swapped on collapse change) pins a collapsed pane to the header
121	///   and floors an expanded pane at `expandedMinHeight` — this is what a drag and a window resize
122	///   respect.
123	/// - The **default** distribution (equal among expanded panes, or the saved weights) is applied via
124	///   `setPosition` after the first real layout and on a workroom switch. Plain window resizes keep
125	///   the user's proportions (native `NSSplitView` behaviour).
126	/// - **Collapsing** a single section keeps the other panes' heights and flexes only a neighbour
127	///   (`reallocateOnToggle`), so a divider the user dragged between two unrelated sections survives a
128	///   collapse elsewhere. **Expanding** a section re-splits the expanded panes **equally**
129	///   (`allocate`) — re-opening a collapsed section returns the stack to equal heights (a third each
130	///   for Changes + History + Pull Request) rather than the minimum floor.
131	/// `NSSplitView` whose dividers use a themed hairline. The system's thin divider can render a hard,
132	/// near-black line between the section panes — most visible while the inspector collapses/expands —
133	/// so we override `dividerColor` to force our subtle border colour on every draw, mid-animation
134	/// included.
135	final class ThemedSplitView: NSSplitView {
136	  override var dividerColor: NSColor {
137	    ThemeService.shared.tokens.nsFg.withAlphaComponent(0.12)
138	  }

145	  // Sized to the installed pane count, which is dynamic: the active activity-bar section decides how
146	  // many sub-sections its pane stacks (3 for Changes + History + Pull Request, 1 for Files). Empty

154	  /// preserving the untouched panes' heights. Both need `bounds.height > 0`, so the work is deferred
155	  /// to `viewDidLayout`.

158	    case redistribute

1	import Foundation

3	/// A VCS action the toolbar can perform.
4	enum VCSRemoteAction: String, Equatable, Sendable, CaseIterable {
5	  case fetch, push, pull, abortRebase
6	
7	  var label: String {
8	    switch self {
9	    case .fetch: return "Fetch"
10	    case .push: return "Push"
11	    case .pull: return "Pull"
12	    case .abortRebase: return "Abort rebase"
13	    }
14	  }
15	
16	}
17	
18	/// Why a remote read or action failed.
19	///
20	/// Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSError`: that enum is the backend-*read* taxonomy
21	/// (`lockContention`/`staleSnapshot`/`partialData`/…) and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)`
22	/// switches over it exhaustively to choose a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge and
23	/// no sensible answer there, so adding it would force a meaningless decision in a function that
24	/// currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`
25	/// beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`.
26	enum VCSRemoteFailure: Equatable, Sendable {
27	  /// `git`/`jj` not on PATH. Distinct from `VCSToolVersions`' floor check, which runs at launch —
28	  /// this is the same condition caught at the point of use.
29	  case toolMissing(String)
30	  case timedOut(VCSRemoteAction)
31	  /// Credentials were needed and none were available.
32	  case authRequired(String)
33	  /// The host's key isn't in `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` turns what would be an interactive
34	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
35	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
36	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
37	  case noRemote
38	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
39	  case rejected(String)
40	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
41	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
42	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
43	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
44	  case rebaseInProgress
45	  /// A repo lock was held — git `index.lock`/`packed-refs.lock`, or jj's `git_import_export.lock`.
46	  ///
47	  /// The payload is the lock file itself when we could find it on disk, and that distinction decides
48	  /// what the UI offers. **`nil` ⇒ transient contention**, so Retry is genuine: another command held the
49	  /// lock briefly and by the next click it is likely gone. **Non-nil ⇒ a lock file is sitting there
50	  /// right now**, and retrying fails identically every time — the same reasoning that makes
51	  /// `rebaseInProgress` offer Abort instead of Retry.
52	  ///
53	  /// A leftover lock is what a SIGKILLed git leaves: the runner escalates to `killTree` two seconds
54	  /// after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's own cleanup never runs.
55	  ///
56	  /// Workroom does NOT delete it. Whether a lock is truly abandoned or held by a git running right now
57	  /// is not knowable from outside the process — `lsof` can't be trusted for it, and removing a live
58	  /// lock corrupts the index — so this reports and explains, and the removal stays the user's call.
59	  /// That is also what git's own message tells you to do.
60	  case locked(VCSLockFile?)
61	  /// jj refused to rewrite a commit protected by `immutable_heads()` — reached by Pull, whose
62	  /// `jj rebase -b @` moves the whole branch containing `@`, and that branch usually contains a
63	  /// remote-tracked commit. Measured on jj 0.43 for a workroom based off a feature branch while trunk
64	  /// moved on: `Error: Commit 4c8e754829da is immutable`.
65	  ///
66	  /// Offers no retry, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the destination doesn't change between clicks, so
67	  /// every retry fails identically. The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base instead of
68	  /// guessing `trunk()` — filed, not built.
69	  case immutableHistory(String)
70	  /// jj refuses to push a commit with an empty description, changes or not. This is the state a workroom
71	  /// sits in the moment you edit a file and before you write a message, so it is the most reachable
72	  /// failure on the push path, not an edge case. Measured: `Error: Won't push commit 050e657d3c36 since
73	  /// it has no description`.
74	  case needsDescription(String)
75	  case other(String)
76	}
77	
78	/// A VCS remote action queued behind a confirmation. Only a pull over a dirty working tree needs one:
79	/// `--autostash` stashes and reapplies, and workroom trees are essentially always dirty, so this fires
80	/// most times someone pulls — the copy has to be worth reading rather than a speed bump.
81	///
82	/// Carries the `SidebarID` it was raised for, and `AppStore.runRemoteAction` verifies it: the dialog is
83	/// not modal to the sidebar, so the selection can move while it is open.
84	struct PendingVCSAction: Identifiable, Equatable, Sendable {
85	  let action: VCSRemoteAction
86	  let sid: SidebarID
87	  var id: String { "\(action.rawValue)-\(sid.hashValue)" }
88	}
89	
90	/// A lock file found blocking a VCS operation.
91	///
92	/// Located by parsing the path out of git's own error, which names it exactly, then stat-ing it — so the
93	/// file reported is the one git actually complained about rather than a guess at which lock it might be.
94	struct VCSLockFile: Equatable, Sendable {
95	  let path: String
96	  let modifiedAt: Date
97	
98	  var filename: String { (path as NSString).lastPathComponent }
99	}
100	
101	/// What a remote-state read decided. Mirrors `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`, `keepPrior` included: a
102	/// transient blip must not blank a good toolbar.
103	enum VCSRemoteResolution: Equatable, Sendable {
104	  case state(VCSRemoteState)
105	  /// Not a git/jj repo, or a repo with no refs at all (a fresh `git init`).
106	  case absent
107	  case keepPrior
108	  case failed(VCSRemoteFailure)
109	}
110	
111	/// What an action decided.
112	///
113	/// There is deliberately no `okWithConflicts`: jj records conflicts *inside* commits and `jj rebase`
114	/// exits 0 when it produces them, so the exit code cannot distinguish them — and the working-copy read
115	/// that could is not safe to make here (it would re-enter `JJSnapshotGate` for the same project root,
116	/// which that type documents as a deadlock). `RemoteStateModel` upgrades a `.ok` pull to "conflicted"
117	/// from the status refresh it already triggers, after the gate has released.
118	enum VCSRemoteActionResult: Equatable, Sendable {
119	  case ok(summary: String)
120	  case failed(VCSRemoteFailure)
121	}
122	
123	/// The seam for VCS operations that **write** — remote state reads plus fetch/push/pull.
124	///
125	/// Separate from `VCSProviding` on purpose. That protocol's doc calls it "the single seam the app
126	/// **reads** VCS data through", and four resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no
127	/// gate. Putting `fetch` there would mean nothing structurally prevented a read path from firing a
128	/// network mutation — the opposite of what `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee. Keeping writes on
129	/// their own protocol also gives the injected `StatusCommandRunning` a home: `GitProvider` and
130	/// `RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one.
131	///
132	/// This is the growth surface for the rest of the VCS write phase (commit/amend, bookmark management,
133	/// the deep jj ops), which is why it's a protocol with a factory rather than one standalone resolver —
134	/// otherwise each later operation re-derives repo kind and wires its own runner.
135	protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
136	  /// Everything the toolbar renders, as ONE coherent snapshot.
137	  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
138	  func fetch(path: String, projectRoot: String, remote: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
139	  /// `anonymousRevision` is used only by jj, and only when `@` carries no bookmark: it is the revision
140	  /// the auto-created `push-<change-id>` bookmark will point at. Compute it with
141	  /// `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(hasChanges:hasDescription:)` — pushing a bare `@` fails when the
142	  /// working copy is empty and undescribed, which is the state a fresh workroom sits in. Ignored by git.
143	  func push(
144	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool,
145	    anonymousRevision: String
146	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
147	  func pullRebase(
148	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
149	    tracking: VCSTracking?
150	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
151	  /// Recover a workroom left mid-rebase. git only; a no-op for jj, whose rebase is atomic and
152	  /// `jj undo`-able.
153	  func abortRebase(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
154	}
155	
156	extension VCS {
157	  /// The writer for a repo, or a typed error for an unsupported path. Mirrors `provider(for:)`, and
158	  /// routes on the same `repoKind(at:)`.
159	  static func writer(
160	    for root: URL, runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(),
161	    makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) },
162	    gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
163	  ) throws -> VCSWriting {
164	    switch repoKind(at: root) {
165	    case .jjColocated, .jjNonColocated:
166	      return CLIVCSWriter(vcs: "jj", runner: runner, makeProvider: makeProvider, gate: gate)
167	    case .plainGit:
168	      return CLIVCSWriter(vcs: "git", runner: runner, makeProvider: makeProvider, gate: gate)
169	    case .unsupported(let reason):
170	      throw VCSError.unsupportedRepo(reason)
171	    }
172	  }
173	}

175	/// `VCSWriting` over the real `git` / `jj` CLIs.
176	///
177	/// **Why the CLI and not the libraries.** SwiftGitX 0.4.0's `fetch`/`push` pass `NULL` for the options
178	/// struct that would carry `git_remote_callbacks.credentials`, so they have no credential path at all —
179	/// HTTPS authentication is impossible through them — and it has no `pull`. Shelling the real binaries
180	/// means the user's own credential helpers, SSH agent and config just work, which is the same bet the
181	/// status layer already makes with `gh`. jj has no Swift API for these at all.
182	///
183	/// Pure `static` arg-builders, parsers and classifiers carry all the semantics, so they are unit-tested
184	/// without spawning anything — the pattern `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` established for exactly
185	/// this reason.
186	///
187	/// ```
188	///                 ┌──────────── every network op ────────────┐
189	///                 │ runNetwork: stdin=/dev/null, BatchMode,   │
190	///                 │ askpass off, SSH_AUTH_SOCK forwarded      │
191	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
192	///                                      │
193	///                 ┌────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
194	///                 │  JJSnapshotGate.run(projectRoot:)         │  git writes too
195	///                 │  NEVER re-enter for the same root         │
196	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
197	///                                      │
198	///     git ─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────── jj
199	///  fetch → PROJECT ROOT (FETCH_HEAD    │   fetch → PROJECT ROOT (a workspace
200	///          is per-worktree; the root   │           has no .git)
201	///          is one shared answer)       │   push  → PROJECT ROOT (bookmarks are
202	///  push  → workroom                    │           repo-global)
203	///  pull  → root (fetch) + workroom     │   pull  → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
204	///  abort → workroom                    │
205	/// ```
206	struct CLIVCSWriter: VCSWriting, Sendable {
207	  /// `"git"` or `"jj"` — resolved once by `VCS.writer(for:)` so no method re-derives it.
208	  let vcs: String
209	  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
210	  /// For `currentRef` only. The app already has a canonical answer including jj `.ancestor` and git
211	  /// `.detached`; re-deriving it from `%(HEAD)` would lose both.
212	  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
213	  /// Serializes writes per project root. Applied to **git** as well as jj: a project's workrooms are
214	  /// `git worktree add` worktrees sharing one `.git`, so a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a
215	  /// workroom wedged in a rebase.
216	  let gate: JJSnapshotGate
217	
218	  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
219	  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
220	  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
221	  /// Generous because SIGKILLing a rebase is the one genuinely unsafe timeout here — it can leave
222	  /// `rebase-merge` behind. `classify` probes for that and reports `.rebaseInProgress`.
223	  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300
224	
225	  // MARK: - Placement
226	
227	  /// Where an operation must run.
228	  ///
229	  /// **fetch always runs at the project root, for both backends.** For jj because a secondary
230	  /// workspace has no `.git` (the rule `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory` already encodes for
231	  /// `gh`). For git because `FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree** — fetching inside a workroom would leave
232	  /// the project and every sibling workroom reading "never fetched" while their remote refs were
233	  /// perfectly fresh. At the root it's one fact every workroom of the project agrees on.
234	  ///
235	  /// **Everything except fetch runs in the workroom, including jj push.** It used to send jj push to the
236	  /// root on the grounds that bookmarks are repo-global. Bookmarks are — but `@` is not: it is
237	  /// WORKSPACE-scoped, resolved against the working directory. So `jj git push --change @` run at the root
238	  /// pushed the ROOT workspace's working copy and left the workroom's commit at home, while still
239	  /// returning `.ok` so the toolbar reported "Pushed to origin".
240	  ///
241	  /// Measured, root holding `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK` and workspace `wsA` holding `WORKROOM-WORK`: the push
242	  /// created `refs/heads/push-<root's change id>` carrying `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK`. Wrong commit published,
243	  /// the user's work never sent, success reported. `--bookmark` works from a secondary workspace too, so
244	  /// nothing needed the root.
245	  ///
246	  /// The integration test could not see this — it passes `path` and `projectRoot` as the same directory,
247	  /// which makes the two indistinguishable. `opDirectoryTests` now pins them as different.
248	  static func opDirectory(_ action: VCSRemoteAction, path: String, projectRoot: String) -> String {
249	    switch action {
250	    case .fetch: return projectRoot
251	    case .push, .pull, .abortRebase: return path
252	    }
253	  }
254	
255	  /// The **common** git directory for a path — the one shared by every worktree of the repo.
256	  ///
257	  /// `.git` is a directory in a normal repo and a FILE in a worktree, containing
258	  /// `gitdir: <repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>`. That per-worktree directory has its own `FETCH_HEAD`,
259	  /// `HEAD` and `index`, so reading `FETCH_HEAD` from it after fetching at the root finds nothing —
260	  /// the root's fetch wrote the root's copy. Stripping the `/worktrees/<name>` suffix gets the shared
261	  /// directory, which is where a root fetch's `FETCH_HEAD` actually lands.
262	  ///
263	  /// Pure string work, no subprocess: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is authoritative but costs a
264	  /// process for something two file reads answer.
265	  static func commonGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
266	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
267	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
268	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
269	      return nil
270	    }
271	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
272	    // A worktree's `.git` file: `gitdir: /abs/or/relative/path`.
273	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
274	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
275	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
276	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
277	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
278	    let gitDir =
279	      raw.hasPrefix("/")
280	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
281	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
282	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`.
283	    let parts = gitDir.standardized.pathComponents
284	    guard let index = parts.lastIndex(of: "worktrees"), index > 0 else { return gitDir }
285	    return URL(fileURLWithPath: "/" + parts[1..<index].joined(separator: "/"))
286	  }
287	
288	  /// `FETCH_HEAD`'s modification time. git rewrites it on **every** fetch, no-ops included (verified),
289	  /// so its mtime is a complete record of git fetches — including one the user ran in a terminal.
290	  static func gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: URL?) -> VCSLastFetch {
291	    guard let dir = commonGitDir else { return .unknown }
292	    let head = dir.appendingPathComponent("FETCH_HEAD")
293	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: head.path) else { return .never }
294	    guard
295	      let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: head.path),
296	      let date = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
