312	  /// Exact two-way divergence, independent of the user's `push.default`.
313	  ///
314	  /// **Deliberately not `%(push:track)`/`%(upstream:track)`.** Under `push.default=simple` — git's
315	  /// built-in default — `%(push)` resolves to nothing for a branch with no upstream, and every
316	  /// workroom is `git worktree add -b`, i.e. has no upstream. Deriving counts from that field leaves
317	  /// the badge permanently blank on any machine not set to `push.default=current` (verified on git
318	  /// 2.55). It also sidesteps a branch whose `%(upstream)` is a *local* branch, which would otherwise
319	  /// produce counts against a ref that isn't on any remote.
320	  ///
321	  /// `A...B` with `--left-right --count` prints `<only in A>\t<only in B>`, so with `A = HEAD` the
322	  /// left number is ahead and the right is behind.
323	  static func gitCountsArgs(remote: String, branch: String) -> [String] {
324	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + [
325	      "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", "HEAD...refs/remotes/\(remote)/\(branch)",
326	    ]
327	  }

330	  /// pass-NULL-and-honour-config philosophy `GitCommitDiff` documents. No `--no-write-fetch-head`
331	  /// either — `FETCH_HEAD` is exactly what `gitLastFetch` reads.
332	  /// `--` closes the option list. See `gitPushArgs` for why every builder in this file does that.
333	  static func gitFetchArgs(remote: String) -> [String] {
334	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["fetch", "--", remote]

337	  /// `--set-upstream` only when there is no counterpart yet; passing it on every push would rewrite
338	  /// `branch.<name>.remote`/`.merge` each time. **Never** `--force`/`--force-with-lease`: a rejection
339	  /// becomes `.rejected` and the UI offers Pull.
340	  ///
341	  /// `--porcelain` is what makes the rejection detectable without reading prose — see
342	  /// `gitPushRejected(stdout:)`. It moves a machine-readable per-ref line onto stdout and leaves
343	  /// stderr's hints alone, so nothing else about the failure path changes.
344	  /// **The branch is sent as a fully-qualified refspec, never as a bare operand.** An argv array stops
345	  /// SHELL injection; it does nothing about OPTION injection, and git parses options that appear after
346	  /// the positional remote.
347	  ///
348	  /// The whole chain is verified on git 2.55, not theorised. `refs/heads/--all` is a legal refname
349	  /// (`check-ref-format` accepts it; only the `--branch` shorthand refuses). A malicious remote that
350	  /// points its `HEAD` at that ref makes `git clone` create a LOCAL branch called `--all`, which is what
351	  /// `git branch --show-current` and therefore `GitProvider.currentRef` then report. Feeding that to
352	  /// `push <remote> <branch>` pushed **every** branch in the repo to the attacker's server — measured:
353	  /// `refs/heads/--all`, `refs/heads/private-work-1`, `refs/heads/private-work-2`. Since every workroom
354	  /// of a project is a `git worktree add -b` in the same repo, that is every workroom's branch. `--mirror`
355	  /// is worse still: it can delete remote refs that are absent locally.
356	  ///
357	  /// A `refs/heads/…:refs/heads/…` refspec cannot present as an option no matter what the name contains,
358	  /// and it also pins the push to this one ref regardless of `push.default`. `--` alone would fix THIS
359	  /// builder, but not the pull one (see `gitPullArgs`), so both use refspecs for one rule.
360	  static func gitPushArgs(branch: String, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool) -> [String] {
361	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["push", "--porcelain"]
362	      + (setUpstream ? ["--set-upstream"] : [])
363	      + ["--", remote, "refs/heads/\(branch):refs/heads/\(branch)"]
364	  }

366	  /// Whether `push --porcelain` reported a rejected ref.
367	  ///
368	  /// Each porcelain line is `<flag>\t<from>:<to>\t<summary>`, and the flag is the contract: `!`
369	  /// rejected, ` ` updated, `*` new ref, `=` up to date, `-` deleted, `+` forced (we never force).
370	  ///
371	  /// This exists because the prose we used to match is translated and the flag is not. Homebrew git
372	  /// 2.55 under `fr_FR.UTF-8` answers `Les mises à jour ont été rejetées …` on stderr while stdout
373	  /// still reads `!\trefs/heads/master:refs/heads/master\t[rejected] (fetch first)` — measured, both
374	  /// locales. `StatusCommandRunner` pins `LC_ALL=C` so the prose match works today; this stops
375	  /// `.rejected` — the one failure whose recovery is a *different action* — depending on that pin.
376	  static func gitPushRejected(stdout: String) -> Bool {
377	    stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).contains { $0.hasPrefix("!\t") }
378	  }

381	  /// without it every pull dies on "cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes". The remote
382	  /// branch is explicit so a workroom with no configured upstream can still pull.

384	  /// **`--` is NOT enough here, which is why the branch is fully qualified.** Measured on git 2.55 with a
385	  /// local branch named `--upload-pack=<script>` (a legal refname, planted by a malicious remote's HEAD
386	  /// as `gitPushArgs` describes): `pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <branch>` ran the script, and so did
387	  /// `pull --rebase --autostash -- <remote> <branch>` — `git pull` forwards the refspec to fetch in a way

389	  /// `fetch -- <remote> <branch>`. So the operand boundary is per-subcommand and cannot be reasoned about
390	  /// from `--` alone; a `refs/heads/` prefix can never look like an option, so that is the rule used.
391	  static func gitPullArgs(remote: String, branch: String) -> [String] {
392	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening

394	  }

409	  /// One record per `(name, remote)` pair.
410	  ///
411	  /// Three verified traps in this template. The keyword is **`self`**, not `ref` (`ref.name()` errors).
412	  /// The `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing —
413	  /// calling `tracking_*_count()` on a local ref renders the literal string
414	  /// `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>` into the output. And a colocated repo has a pseudo-remote
415	  /// called `git` that `--all-remotes` includes, which `parseJJBookmarks` drops.
416	  static func jjBookmarkListArgs() -> [String] {
417	    let template = """
418	      self.name() \
419	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.remote(), self.remote(), "") \
420	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.present() && !self.conflict(), self.normal_target().commit_id(), "") \
421	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.present(), "1", "0") \
422	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.conflict(), "1", "0") \
423	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.tracked(), "1", "0") \
424	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present(), \
425	      self.tracking_ahead_count().lower(), "") \
426	      ++ "\\x00" ++ if(self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present(), \
427	      self.tracking_behind_count().lower(), "") \
428	      ++ "\\n"
429	      """
430	    return ["bookmark", "list", "--all-remotes"] + jjReadFlags + ["-T", template]
431	  }

446	  /// Quote a name for interpolation into a revset.
447	  ///
448	  /// Bare interpolation is a real parse bug, not a hypothetical. Verified against jj 0.43: a remote
449	  /// named `a b`, `a)b` or `a:b` fails outright (`Failed to parse revset: Syntax error`), and — worse —
450	  /// `a|b` *succeeds* as the UNION of two patterns, so the count comes back wrong with no error to
451	  /// notice. Quoting fixes all of them.
452	  ///
453	  /// `\` is escaped before `"`, so the backslash pass cannot re-escape the escapes the quote pass adds.
454	  static func jjQuote(_ name: String) -> String {
455	    let escaped = name.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\", with: "\\\\")
456	      .replacingOccurrences(of: "\"", with: "\\\"")

460	  /// The base an unbookmarked `@` is measured — and rebased — against.
461	  ///
462	  /// `trunk()` is jj's own alias, so this defers to the user's `revset-aliases.'trunk()'` when they've
463	  /// set one and to jj's default (the latest of `main`/`master`/`trunk` on a remote) when they haven't.
464	  /// Verified to degrade quietly: in a repo whose only remote bookmark was `weird-name`, `trunk()`
465	  /// resolved without error and `@..trunk()` counted 0, so an unusual repo reports "not behind" rather
466	  /// than a failure.

468	  /// One literal, shared by `jjBehindRevset` and `jjRebaseDestination`, because the count and the button
469	  /// have to mean the same thing.

471	
472	  /// Commits of ours that no remote bookmark has — what a push would send.
473	  ///
474	  /// Scoped to ALL of the remote's bookmarks on purpose, unlike `jjBehindRevset`: a commit already
475	  /// reachable from some other remote branch IS pushed, so it must not count as ahead.
476	  ///
477	  /// The `~(empty() && description(exact:""))` filter is `jjPushRevision`'s rule expressed as a revset —
478	  /// jj won't push a commit with no changes AND no description, and a workroom's `@` after `jj new` is
479	  /// exactly that, so without this every clean workroom read as "1 to push". `~empty()` alone is NOT
480	  /// equivalent and undercounts: describe an empty `@` and jj will push it while `~empty()` reports 0.
481	  /// Both measured on jj 0.43.
482	  static func jjAheadRevset(remote: String) -> String {
483	    "(remote_bookmarks(remote=\(jjQuote(remote)))..@) & ~(empty() & description(exact:\"\"))"
484	  }

486	  /// Commits on the main line that we don't have — what a pull would bring.
487	  ///
488	  /// **Measured against `trunk()`, not against every remote bookmark.** It used to be
489	  /// `@..remote_bookmarks(remote=…)`, which counts every commit on every remote branch that isn't in
490	  /// `@`'s ancestry — so a repo with unmerged feature branches reported their commits as "to pull" while
491	  /// sitting exactly on the tip of master. Reproduced on jj 0.43: with `@-` equal to `master@origin`,
492	  /// origin holding master and one unmerged `feat`, that revset counted 3 and named `feat1`/`feat2`/
493	  /// `feat3`; `@..trunk()` counted 0. The equivalent git query has always been scoped to one branch
494	  /// (`HEAD...refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`), so this also ends an asymmetry between the backends.
495	  static let jjBehindRevset = "@..\(jjTrunkRevset)"

497	  /// Where a jj pull rebases `@`.
498	  ///
499	  /// A bookmarked `@` goes onto its own remote counterpart. An unbookmarked one has no counterpart —
500	  /// `VCSTracking.comparedTo` carries the bare remote name as the sentinel for that state — and goes onto
501	  /// `trunk()`, the same base its behind count is measured from.
502	  ///
503	  /// That second case used to return early without rebasing at all, so Pull fetched and stopped: the
504	  /// toolbar offered "Pull" beside a count the button could not act on. git's Pull has always been
505	  /// pull-and-rebase, and this is what makes jj's the same operation.
506	  static func jjRebaseDestination(comparedTo: String?, remote: String) -> String {
507	    guard let comparedTo, comparedTo != remote else { return jjTrunkRevset }
508	    return comparedTo
509	  }

544	  struct RemoteRefs: Equatable, Sendable {
545	    /// Remote names, first-seen order (so `origin` keeps its natural primacy when present).
546	    let remotes: [String]
547	    /// Short names, e.g. `"origin/main"`.
548	    let shortNames: Set<String>
549	  }
550	
551	  /// Parse `for-each-ref refs/remotes` output.
552	  ///
553	  /// Skips records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, whose short
554	  /// name is the bare remote and which would otherwise look like a branch called `origin`.
555	  /// Field count is checked rather than assumed: a ref name can't contain a control character, but
556	  /// being strict here means a malformed line is dropped rather than crashing the read.
557	  static func parseGitRemoteRefs(_ stdout: String) -> RemoteRefs {
558	    var remotes: [String] = []
559	    var shortNames: Set<String> = []
560	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
561	      let fields = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
562	      guard fields.count == 3 else { continue }
563	      guard fields[2].isEmpty else { continue }  // symref → origin/HEAD
564	      let refname = fields[0]
565	      let prefix = "refs/remotes/"
566	      guard refname.hasPrefix(prefix) else { continue }
567	      let short = String(refname.dropFirst(prefix.count))
568	      guard let slash = short.firstIndex(of: "/") else { continue }
569	      let remote = String(short[short.startIndex..<slash])
570	      guard !remote.isEmpty, slash < short.index(before: short.endIndex) else { continue }
571	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
572	      shortNames.insert(short)
573	    }
574	    return RemoteRefs(remotes: remotes, shortNames: shortNames)
575	  }

577	  /// `"3\t1"` → (ahead: 3, behind: 1). `nil` for anything unexpected — never a misleading zero.
578	  static func parseCounts(_ stdout: String) -> (ahead: Int, behind: Int)? {
579	    let fields = stdout.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
580	      .split(whereSeparator: { $0 == "\t" || $0 == " " })
581	    guard fields.count == 2, let ahead = Int(fields[0]), let behind = Int(fields[1]) else {
582	      return nil
583	    }
584	    return (ahead, behind)
585	  }

587	  /// One bookmark, folded from its local row and its `@<remote>` row.
588	  struct JJBookmark: Equatable, Sendable {
589	    let name: String
590	    let tracking: VCSTracking?
591	  }
592	
593	  /// Parse `bookmark list --all-remotes` output into per-name tracking, plus the remote names.
594	  ///
595	  /// **jj's counts are inverted relative to git and are swapped here.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an
596	  /// `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local*, which is git's **behind** — jj's own default
597	  /// template proves it by printing "ahead by N commits" next to `@origin`. One line, one comment, and
598	  /// a cross-backend integration test pins it.
599	  static func parseJJBookmarks(_ stdout: String) -> (bookmarks: [JJBookmark], remotes: [String]) {
600	    var remotes: [String] = []
601	    var trackingByName: [String: VCSTracking] = [:]
602	    var localNames: [String] = []
603	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
604	      let f = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
605	      guard f.count == 8 else { continue }
606	      let (name, remote) = (f[0], f[1])
607	      let present = f[3] == "1"
608	      let tracked = f[5] == "1"
609	      guard !name.isEmpty else { continue }
610	      if remote.isEmpty {
611	        if !localNames.contains(name) { localNames.append(name) }
612	        continue
613	      }
614	      // A colocated repo exposes a pseudo-remote called `git` (jj's local git-tracking bookmarks).
615	      // It is not a remote, and including it would both pollute the remote list and produce counts
616	      // against the local git refs rather than a server.
617	      guard remote != "git" else { continue }
618	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
619	      // An untracked remote bookmark, or one deleted on the remote, cannot answer counts. `gone`
620	      // reports the deletion; nil counts report "unanswerable" rather than a misleading zero.
621	      let jjAhead = Int(f[6])
622	      let jjBehind = Int(f[7])
623	      trackingByName[name] = VCSTracking(
624	        comparedTo: "\(name)@\(remote)",
625	        ahead: tracked && present ? jjBehind : nil,  // swapped — see the doc comment
626	        behind: tracked && present ? jjAhead : nil,
627	        gone: !present)
628	    }
629	    let bookmarks = localNames.map { JJBookmark(name: $0, tracking: trackingByName[$0]) }
630	    return (bookmarks, remotes)
631	  }

633	  /// The newest operation whose description says it fetched.
634	  ///
635	  /// Matches a prefix rather than the whole string so a reworded suffix survives. The failure mode is
636	  /// graceful — one absent label, never a wrong one — and an integration test reddens on a jj bump.
637	  ///
638	  /// **Incomplete by design**: a `jj git fetch` that brings nothing prints "Nothing changed." and
639	  /// records NO operation (verified, jj 0.43), so this answers "last fetch that changed something".
640	  /// `RemoteStateModel` takes the max of this and Workroom's own recorded fetch time to close the gap.
641	  static func parseJJFetchOp(_ stdout: String) -> Date? {
642	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
643	      let f = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
644	      guard f.count == 2, f[1].hasPrefix("fetch from git remote") else { continue }
645	      guard let seconds = TimeInterval(f[0]) else { continue }
646	      return Date(timeIntervalSince1970: seconds)
647	    }
648	    return nil
649	  }

651	  // MARK: - Classification
652	
653	  /// Map a failed command to a typed failure. `nil` means success.
654	  ///
655	  /// `gitDir` lets a failed pull be upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` — the distinction matters because
656	  /// that state must offer Abort, not Retry.
657	  static func classify(
658	    _ result: CommandResult, action: VCSRemoteAction, tool: String,
659	    gitDir: URL? = nil
660	  ) -> VCSRemoteFailure? {
661	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .toolMissing(tool) }
662	    let err = result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout
663	    // A timed-out pull may have left a rebase behind; that reads better than "timed out".
664	    if result.timedOut {
665	      if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
666	      return .timedOut(action)
667	    }
668	    guard !result.ok else { return nil }
669	    if err.contains("Host key verification failed") || err.contains("REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION") {
670	      return .hostKeyUnverified(err)
671	    }
672	    if err.contains("terminal prompts disabled") || err.contains("could not read Username")
673	      || err.contains("could not read Password") || err.contains("Authentication failed")
674	      || err.contains("Permission denied (publickey)")
675	    {
676	      return .authRequired(err)
677	    }
678	    if err.contains("would be overwritten") { return .dirtyWorkingTree(err) }
679	    if err.contains("does not appear to be a git repository") || err.contains("No such remote")
680	      || err.contains("no such remote") || err.contains("No git remotes")
681	    {
682	      return .noRemote
683	    }
684	    // Flag column first, prose second. The string checks stay as a fallback rather than being replaced:
685	    // `--porcelain` is ours to pass on the push path only, so a rejection surfaced by any other route
686	    // (a remote helper, a future caller that forgets the flag) still classifies.
687	    if gitPushRejected(stdout: result.stdout) || err.contains("Updates were rejected")
688	      || err.contains("! [rejected]")
689	    {
690	      return .rejected(err)
691	    }
692	    // Both jj-only, and both permanent until the user acts — so they must NOT reach `.other`, whose
693	    // recovery is a retry of the same doomed command. jj doesn't localize, so matching its prose is safe
694	    // here in a way it wouldn't be for git.
695	    if err.contains("since it has no description") || err.contains("has no description") {
696	      return .needsDescription(err)
697	    }
698	    if err.contains("is immutable") || err.contains("immutable commits") {
699	      return .immutableHistory(err)
700	    }
701	    if err.contains("Failed to take lock for Git import/export")
702	      || (err.contains(".lock")
703	        && (err.contains("could not be obtained") || err.contains("File exists")
704	          || err.contains("Unable to create")))
705	    {
706	      return .locked(lockFile(in: err))
707	    }
708	    if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
709	    // A lock failure that never names a lock. git's message depends on WHICH internal step hit the lock:
710	    // a fast-forward pull reports `Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`, but a pull that must really
711	    // rebase fails in autostash first and says only `error: could not write index` / `fatal: Cannot
712	    // autostash` — no path, no "lock", nothing the checks above can match. That is the diverged pull,
713	    // i.e. exactly what the toolbar's Pull button is for, and it was landing in `.other` with raw stderr.
714	    //
715	    // So when the symptoms are lock-shaped, ask the DISK instead of the message. Deliberately last: any
716	    // failure git explains properly keeps its own classification, and this only speaks for the ones it
717	    // doesn't.
718	    if lockSymptom(err), let lock = existingLockFile(gitDir: gitDir) { return .locked(lock) }
719	    let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
720	    return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
721	  }
722	
723	  /// Whether a rebase is parked in this worktree. Both directory names are checked: `rebase-merge` for
724	  /// an interactive/merge rebase, `rebase-apply` for the am-based one.
725	  static func rebaseInProgress(gitDir: URL?) -> Bool {
726	    guard let gitDir else { return false }
727	    let fm = FileManager.default
728	    return fm.fileExists(atPath: gitDir.appendingPathComponent("rebase-merge").path)
729	      || fm.fileExists(atPath: gitDir.appendingPathComponent("rebase-apply").path)
730	  }
731	
732	  /// The lock file a failure is complaining about, or nil if we can't point at one.
733	  ///
734	  /// The path is taken from git's OWN message rather than guessed: git names the exact file it couldn't
735	  /// create (`fatal: Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`), and a repo has several lock files that
736	  /// mean different things — `index.lock`, `packed-refs.lock`, `HEAD.lock`, `config.lock`. Naming the
737	  /// wrong one would send someone to delete a file that isn't the problem.
738	  ///
739	  /// Returns nil for jj's import/export lock, whose message carries no path, and — deliberately — when
740	  /// the named file no longer exists: a lock that cleared between the failure and this check WAS
741	  /// transient contention, which is exactly the case where Retry is the right offer.
742	  static func lockFile(in stderr: String) -> VCSLockFile? {
743	    guard let path = parseLockPath(stderr) else { return nil }
744	    guard let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: path),
745	      let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
746	    else { return nil }
747	    return VCSLockFile(path: path, modifiedAt: modified)
748	  }
749	
750	  /// Whether a failure LOOKS like it was caused by a lock, without saying so.
751	  ///
752	  /// Narrow on purpose. These are the symptoms git reports when it fails to take a lock through a path
753	  /// that doesn't print the lock's name; anything broader would start blaming a lock file that happens to
754	  /// exist for failures it had nothing to do with.
755	  static func lockSymptom(_ stderr: String) -> Bool {
756	    stderr.contains("could not write index") || stderr.contains("Cannot autostash")
757	      || stderr.contains("cannot lock ref") || stderr.contains("Unable to write")
758	  }
759	
760	  /// The lock files a repo can be blocked by, newest-relevant first. `index.lock` lives in the WORKTREE's
761	  /// own git dir; `packed-refs.lock` and `config.lock` live in the COMMON dir that every worktree shares.
762	  static let knownLockNames = ["index.lock", "packed-refs.lock", "HEAD.lock", "config.lock"]
763	
764	  /// The first lock file actually present in this repo, checking both the worktree's git dir and the
765	  /// common one — a workroom is a `git worktree`, so its `index.lock` and the repo's `packed-refs.lock`
766	  /// are in different directories.
767	  static func existingLockFile(gitDir: URL?) -> VCSLockFile? {
768	    guard let gitDir else { return nil }
769	    let fm = FileManager.default
770	    var dirs = [gitDir]
771	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`. Cheap and string-only; `commonGitDir` does the same trip
772	    // from a path rather than from an already-resolved git dir.
773	    if gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().lastPathComponent == "worktrees" {
774	      dirs.append(gitDir.deletingLastPathComponent().deletingLastPathComponent())
775	    }
776	    for dir in dirs {
777	      for name in knownLockNames {
778	        let candidate = dir.appendingPathComponent(name)
779	        guard let attrs = try? fm.attributesOfItem(atPath: candidate.path),
780	          let modified = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
781	        else { continue }
782	        return VCSLockFile(path: candidate.path, modifiedAt: modified)
783	      }
784	    }
785	    return nil
786	  }
787	
788	  /// The quoted path out of git's lock errors. Pure, so the parsing is testable without a repo.
789	  ///
790	  /// Covers both phrasings that quote a path — the bare `Unable to create '<path>'` and the ref-update
791	  /// form (`error: cannot lock ref 'refs/…': Unable to create '<path>.lock': File exists`), which nests
792	  /// two quoted strings and must yield the second.
793	  static func parseLockPath(_ stderr: String) -> String? {
794	    guard let marker = stderr.range(of: "Unable to create '") else { return nil }
795	    let rest = stderr[marker.upperBound...]
796	    guard let close = rest.firstIndex(of: "'") else { return nil }
797	    let path = String(rest[..<close])
798	    // Only ever report an absolute path to a `.lock`: a relative one would be meaningless to a user
799	    // reading it out of a tooltip, and a non-`.lock` match means the phrasing wasn't what we assumed.
800	    guard path.hasPrefix("/"), path.hasSuffix(".lock") else { return nil }
801	    return path
802	  }
803	
804	  /// This worktree's OWN git directory — `<common>/worktrees/<name>` for a workroom, the same as the
805	  /// common dir for a project root. Rebase state (`rebase-merge`), `HEAD` and `index` live here, unlike
806	  /// `FETCH_HEAD` which `commonGitDir` deliberately resolves to the shared copy.
807	  static func worktreeGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
808	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
809	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
810	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
811	      return nil
812	    }
813	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
814	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
815	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
816	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
817	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
818	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
819	    return raw.hasPrefix("/")
820	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
821	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
822	  }

828	  ) async -> CommandResult {

834	  /// Run a write through the per-project gate.
835	  ///
836	  /// `JJSnapshotGate`'s doc warns against timing the innermost call, because `withTimeout` cannot
837	  /// cancel a blocking jj-lib call and the gate would release while the abandoned call still held the
838	  /// lock. That reasoning does **not** apply to a subprocess: `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at
839	  /// `+timeout` and `ProcessTree.killTree`s at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone and its
840	  /// locks genuinely released. Hence the runner's own timeout with no outer `withTimeout` — this looks
841	  /// like a violation of that doc and isn't.
842	  private func gated(
843	    _ projectRoot: String, _ body: @Sendable @escaping () async -> CommandResult
844	  ) async -> CommandResult? {
845	    try? await gate.run(projectRoot: projectRoot, body)
846	  }

850	  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution {
851	    let root = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true)
852	    let current: VCSRef
853	    do {
854	      current = try await makeProvider(root).currentRef(root: root)
855	    } catch {
856	      return .failed(.other("couldn't read the current ref: \(error)"))
857	    }

863	  private func gitRemoteState(path: String, current: VCSRef) async -> VCSRemoteResolution {
864	    let refs = await run(Self.gitRemoteRefsArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
865	    if let failure = Self.classify(refs, action: .fetch, tool: "git") {
866	      // A blip must not blank a good toolbar; a missing tool or a real error should show.
867	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
868	      return .failed(failure)
869	    }
870	    let parsed = Self.parseGitRemoteRefs(refs.stdout)
871	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(parsed.remotes)
872	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
873	    if let primary, let branch = current.name, current.kind == .branch {
874	      let counterpart = "\(primary)/\(branch)"
875	      if parsed.shortNames.contains(counterpart) {
876	        let counts = await run(
877	          Self.gitCountsArgs(remote: primary, branch: branch), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
878	        if let parsedCounts = Self.parseCounts(counts.stdout) {
879	          tracking = VCSTracking(
880	            comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: parsedCounts.ahead, behind: parsedCounts.behind,
881	            gone: false)
882	        } else {
883	          tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: false)
884	        }
885	      } else {
886	        // No counterpart on the remote — the normal state of a fresh workroom, since
887	        // `git worktree add -b` sets no upstream. Reported as `gone` so the toolbar offers Publish.
888	        tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: true)
889	      }
890	    }
891	    return .state(
892	      VCSRemoteState(
893	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: parsed.remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
894	        lastFetch: Self.gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: Self.commonGitDir(at: path)),
895	        resolvedAt: Date()))
896	  }
897	
898	  private func jjRemoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef) async
899	    -> VCSRemoteResolution
900	  {
901	    // Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated.
902	    let list = await run(Self.jjBookmarkListArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
903	    if let failure = Self.classify(list, action: .fetch, tool: "jj") {
904	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
905	      return .failed(failure)
906	    }
907	    let parsed = Self.parseJJBookmarks(list.stdout)
908	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(parsed.remotes)
909	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
910	    if let primary {
911	      switch current.kind {
912	      case .branch:
913	        tracking = current.name.flatMap { name in
914	          parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }?.tracking
915	        }
916	      // `.none` belongs with `.ancestor`, and leaving it out was a bug that hid the exact case this
917	      // toolbar exists for. `jj git fetch` fast-forwards a tracked local bookmark, so as soon as the
918	      // main line moves, an unbookmarked `@`'s ancestry contains no bookmark at all and `currentRef`
919	      // drops from `.ancestor` to `.none`. Sending that to `tracking = nil` meant the counts, the pills
920	      // and `canPull` all vanished at the moment the workroom first became behind — the toolbar went
921	      // quiet precisely when it had something to say. The revsets below never needed a bookmark to
922	      // begin with; `.detached` still yields nil, since that's git's shape and has no jj meaning.
923	      case .ancestor, .none:
924	        // `@` carries no bookmark — the normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates
925	        // no bookmark. The bookmark row's counts would describe the ANCESTOR, not the user's work, so
926	        // count the actual revsets instead. The two are deliberately scoped differently: ahead against
927	        // every remote bookmark (anything already pushed anywhere isn't ahead), behind against `trunk()`
928	        // alone (see `jjBehindRevset` — the all-bookmarks form counted other branches' work as ours to
929	        // pull). Both agree with what the buttons do: `jjPushRevision` and `jjRebaseDestination`.
930	        let ahead = await run(
931	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjAheadRevset(remote: primary)), in: path, timeout: refTimeout
932	        )
933	        let behind = await run(
934	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjBehindRevset), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
935	        tracking = VCSTracking(
936	          comparedTo: primary,
937	          ahead: ahead.ok ? Self.countLines(ahead.stdout) : nil,
938	          behind: behind.ok ? Self.countLines(behind.stdout) : nil,
939	          gone: false)
940	      case .detached:
941	        tracking = nil
942	      }
943	    }
944	    // jj's fetch is invisible to `FETCH_HEAD` (it passes `--no-write-fetch-head`), so scan the op log.
945	    let ops = await run(Self.jjOpLogArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
946	    let lastFetch = ops.ok ? Self.parseJJFetchOp(ops.stdout) : nil
947	    return .state(
948	      VCSRemoteState(
949	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: parsed.remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
950	        lastFetch: lastFetch.map { .at($0) } ?? (ops.ok ? .never : .unknown),
951	        resolvedAt: Date()))
952	  }

967	    let dir = Self.opDirectory(.fetch, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
968	    let args = vcs == "jj" ? Self.jjFetchArgs(remote: remote) : Self.gitFetchArgs(remote: remote)
969	    guard
970	      let result = await gated(

972	        { [self] in

974	        })
975	    else { return .failed(.other("fetch was cancelled")) }
976	    if let failure = Self.classify(
977	      result, action: .fetch, tool: vcs, gitDir: Self.worktreeGitDir(at: path))

984	  func push(
985	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool,
986	    anonymousRevision: String
987	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult {
988	    let dir = Self.opDirectory(.push, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
989	    let args: [String]
990	    if vcs == "jj" {
991	      if current.kind == .branch, let bookmark = current.name {
992	        args = Self.jjPushBookmarkArgs(bookmark: bookmark, remote: remote)
993	      } else {
994	        // Unbookmarked `@`: let jj mint and track a `push-<change-id>` bookmark.
995	        args = Self.jjPushChangeArgs(revision: anonymousRevision, remote: remote)
996	      }
997	    } else {
998	      guard let branch = current.name, current.kind == .branch else {
999	        return .failed(.other("HEAD is detached — check out a branch before pushing."))
1000	      }
1001	      args = Self.gitPushArgs(branch: branch, remote: remote, setUpstream: setUpstream)
1002	    }
1003	    guard
1004	      let result = await gated(
1005	        projectRoot,
1006	        { [self] in
1007	          await run(args, in: dir, timeout: pushTimeout, network: true)
1008	        })
1009	    else { return .failed(.other("push was cancelled")) }
1010	    if let failure = Self.classify(
1011	      result, action: .push, tool: vcs, gitDir: Self.worktreeGitDir(at: path))
1012	    {
1013	      return .failed(failure)
1014	    }
1015	    return .ok(summary: "Pushed to \(remote)")
1016	  }

1018	  func pullRebase(
1019	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
1020	    tracking: VCSTracking?
1021	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult {
1022	    // Both backends fetch first, at the project root, for the reasons `opDirectory` documents. For git
1023	    // `pull` would fetch too, but doing it explicitly at the root keeps `FETCH_HEAD` — and so the
1024	    // "last fetched" label — correct for every workroom of the project.
1025	    // Hoisted above the fetch: BOTH steps classify against it, since a lock can block either one.
1026	    let gitDir = Self.worktreeGitDir(at: path)
1027	    let fetchDir = Self.opDirectory(.fetch, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1028	    let fetchArgs =
1029	      vcs == "jj" ? Self.jjFetchArgs(remote: remote) : Self.gitFetchArgs(remote: remote)
1030	    guard
1031	      let fetched = await gated(
1032	        projectRoot,
1033	        { [self] in
1034	          await run(fetchArgs, in: fetchDir, timeout: fetchTimeout, network: true)
1035	        })
1036	    else { return .failed(.other("pull was cancelled")) }
1037	    if let failure = Self.classify(fetched, action: .pull, tool: vcs, gitDir: gitDir) {
1038	      return .failed(failure)
1039	    }
1040	
1041	    let dir = Self.opDirectory(.pull, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1042	    let args: [String]
1043	    if vcs == "jj" {
1044	      // Always rebases now. An unbookmarked `@` falls back to `trunk()` rather than returning early:
1045	      // fetching moves the remote bookmarks but does NOT move `@`, so stopping there left the workroom
1046	      // as far behind as it started while the toolbar went on offering Pull. Already a descendant of the
1047	      // destination is not an error — jj prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
1048	      args = Self.jjRebaseArgs(
1049	        onto: Self.jjRebaseDestination(comparedTo: tracking?.comparedTo, remote: remote))
1050	    } else {
1051	      guard let branch = Self.pullBranch(current: current, tracking: tracking) else {
1052	        return .failed(.other("no remote branch to pull from."))
1053	      }
1054	      args = Self.gitPullArgs(remote: remote, branch: branch)
1055	    }
1056	    guard
1057	      let result = await gated(
1058	        projectRoot,
1059	        { [self] in
1060	          await run(args, in: dir, timeout: pullTimeout, network: true)
1061	        })
1062	    else { return .failed(.other("pull was cancelled")) }
1063	    if let failure = Self.classify(result, action: .pull, tool: vcs, gitDir: gitDir) {
1064	      return .failed(failure)
1065	    }
1066	    return .ok(summary: "Pulled from \(remote)")
1067	  }

1069	  /// The remote branch a pull rebases from: the counterpart's own name, stripped of its `<remote>/`
1070	  /// prefix, falling back to the local branch name (the same-name convention).
1071	  static func pullBranch(current: VCSRef, tracking: VCSTracking?) -> String? {
1072	    if let comparedTo = tracking?.comparedTo, let slash = comparedTo.firstIndex(of: "/") {
1073	      return String(comparedTo[comparedTo.index(after: slash)...])
1074	    }
1075	    return current.name
1076	  }

1078	  func abortRebase(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult {
1079	    guard vcs != "jj" else {
1080	      // jj's rebase is atomic and undoable — there is no half-finished state to abort.
1081	      return .ok(summary: "Nothing to abort")
1082	    }
1083	    let dir = Self.opDirectory(.abortRebase, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1084	    guard
1085	      let result = await gated(
1086	        projectRoot,
1087	        { [self] in
1088	          await run(Self.gitAbortRebaseArgs(), in: dir, timeout: refTimeout)
1089	        })
1090	    else { return .failed(.other("abort was cancelled")) }
1091	    if let failure = Self.classify(result, action: .abortRebase, tool: vcs) {
1092	      return .failed(failure)
1093	    }
1094	    return .ok(summary: "Rebase aborted")
1095	  }

632	  /// Run a VCS remote action for the toolbar's current target, supplying the two facts only the store
633	  /// knows.
634	  ///
635	  /// `setUpstream` for git: a workroom is `git worktree add -b`, so it has no counterpart on the remote
636	  /// until its first push — that first push is the one that should establish tracking, and later ones
637	  /// must not keep rewriting `branch.<name>.remote`.
638	  ///
639	  /// `anonymousRevision` for jj: `jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark, so `@` is unbookmarked
640	  /// and the push goes through jj's `--change` path. Pushing a bare `@` fails when the working copy is
641	  /// empty AND undescribed — exactly the state a fresh workroom sits in — so the revision falls back to
642	  /// its parent. The working-copy facts come from the status sweep, at no extra cost.
643	  /// Request a remote action, confirming first when one is needed.
644	  ///
645	  /// **The confirmation gate lives HERE, not in the toolbar.** It used to sit in `VCSToolbar.perform`,
646	  /// which meant the Source Control menu's ⌥⇧⌘P went straight past it: the button warned before
647	  /// autostashing a dirty tree and the keyboard shortcut didn't. A safety gate that only one of two
648	  /// entry points honours isn't a gate, so every caller funnels through this.
649	  func performRemoteAction(_ action: VCSRemoteAction) {
650	    guard let target = remoteState.target else { return }
651	    // A pull rewrites the working copy, and workroom trees are essentially always dirty — `--autostash`
652	    // will stash and reapply, which is worth saying before it happens.
653	    if action == .pull, workroomStatuses[target.sid]?.dirty == true {
654	      pendingRemoteConfirm = PendingVCSAction(action: action, sid: target.sid)
655	      return
656	    }
657	    runRemoteAction(action, on: target.sid)
658	  }
659	
660	  /// Run a confirmed action against the workroom it was confirmed FOR.
661	  ///
662	  /// The `sid` is checked rather than trusted: the confirmation dialog is not modal to the sidebar, so
663	  /// the selection can move while it is open. Re-deriving the target at click time would silently run
664	  /// the pull against a different workroom than the one the dirty-tree warning described.
665	  func runRemoteAction(_ action: VCSRemoteAction, on sid: SidebarID) {
666	    guard let target = remoteState.target, target.sid == sid else { return }
667	    guard vcsAllowsRemoteActions(vcs: target.vcs) else { return }
668	    let workingCopy = workroomStatuses[target.sid]?.jjWorkingCopy
669	    let revision = CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(
670	      hasChanges: !(workingCopy?.files.isEmpty ?? true),
671	      hasDescription: !((workingCopy?.description ?? "").isEmpty))
672	    remoteState.perform(
673	      action, setUpstream: remoteState.snapshot?.tracking?.gone == true,
674	      anonymousRevision: revision)
675	  }

678	  ///
679	  /// Called when projects land (so "is any project jj?" is answerable) rather than from `init`. Inert
680	  /// in fixture mode: a UI test's PATH is whatever the runner inherited, and a version toast would
681	  /// overlay the surfaces under test.
682	  ///
683	  /// Also inert under XCTest — `apply` runs in dozens of unit tests, and each would otherwise spawn a
684	  /// real `git --version` and mutate the process-wide cache. Same guard, and the same reason, as the
685	  /// `ShellEnvironment.refresh()` skip in `WorkroomApp.init`. `VCSToolVersionsTests` drives the probe
686	  /// directly with a stub runner.
687	  func refreshVCSToolReport() {
688	    guard !UITestFixture.isActive,
689	      ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] == nil
690	    else { return }
691	    let probeJJ = projects.contains { $0.vcs == "jj" }
692	    Task { [weak self] in
693	      let report = await VCSToolVersionCache.shared.report(probeJJ: probeJJ)
694	      self?.vcsToolReport = report

698	  /// Browser-style back/forward history of visited `(target, tab)` locations (issue #26).
699	  /// `@Published` so toolbar/menu enablement (`canGoBack`/`canGoForward`) re-evaluates when it
700	  /// changes. Session-only — deliberately not persisted across launches. `private(set)` so unit

# Commit box in the Changes inspector

## Context

The Changes inspector shows what changed but offers no way to act on it — committing means
switching to a terminal, retyping the branch context from memory, and writing the message by hand.
This adds a commit box at the bottom of the Changes section, visible whenever the workroom has
uncommitted changes: a single-line **Summary** field, an optional multi-line **Description**, a
**Generate commit message** button that drafts both from the actual diff via the agent CLI, and a
**Commit** button that writes.

The app has never written a commit before, but it is not starting from zero:
`Core/VCSWriting.swift` already shells `git`/`jj` for fetch/push/pull behind the `VCSWriting`
protocol, gated per project root by `JJSnapshotGate` — and its own doc calls itself *"the growth
surface for the rest of the VCS write phase (commit/amend, …)"*. The commit lands there.
`Core/AgentRunner.swift` already runs a headless, zero-tools `claude --print --output-format json`
and parses its envelope. Both are reused rather than reinvented.

Decisions taken with the user: commit for real (not UI-only); jj gets a split button (**Commit** =
`jj commit`, menu item **Describe** = `jj describe`); git writes via the `git` CLI (so pre-commit
hooks, `commit.gpgsign`, `commit.template` and staged deletions all behave as in the user's own
terminal — SwiftGitX's public API cannot stage deletions and libgit2 runs no hooks); the box is
**pinned to the bottom** of the Changes section with the file list scrolling above it.

Agent-backend choice was deferred. This plan uses the proven `claude` headless path only, behind a
seam (`AgentRunning`) so honouring `Defaults[.terminalAgentBackend]` later is a localised change.
`codex` has no zero-tools mode and no `codex exec` argv exists anywhere yet — that stays out.

## 1. The write path — `Core/VCSWriting.swift`

Add to the `VCSWriting` protocol and implement in `CLIVCSWriter` (which already resolves
`vcs == "git" | "jj"` via `VCS.writer(for:)`):

```swift
func commit(path: String, projectRoot: String, message: String, mode: VCSCommitMode) async
  -> VCSCommitResult
```

- `enum VCSCommitMode { case commit, describe }` — `.describe` is jj-only; git ignores it (or the
  UI never offers it, which is the plan).
- New pure static arg builders beside the existing ones, each with the same doc-comment rigour:
  - `gitStageAllArgs()` → `gitHardening + ["add", "--all"]` (stages adds, modifications **and**
    deletions, honouring `.gitignore`). Verify at implementation whether a trailing `--` with no
    pathspec still means whole-tree; drop it if not.
  - `gitCommitArgs(message:)` → `gitHardening + ["commit", "--message", message]`. The message is
    the bound value of `--message`, so it can never be re-parsed as an option — no `refs/heads/`
    style hardening needed here, unlike `gitPushArgs`.
  - `jjDescribeArgs(message:)` → `["describe", "-m", message] + jjWriteFlags`
  - `jjCommitArgs(message:)` → `["commit", "-m", message] + jjWriteFlags`
  - **`jjWriteFlags`, never `jjReadFlags`** — the snapshot is what carries the on-disk edits into
    `@` before it is described/committed.
- Runs in the **workroom** directory (`path`), and through `gated(projectRoot) { … }` for both
  backends — same reasoning `CLIVCSWriter` already documents for git (worktrees share one `.git`).
- git is two gated commands: stage, then commit. If staging fails, return without committing.
- Timeout: a new `commitTimeout` (~120s). Generous on purpose — a pre-commit hook or a `gpg`
  pinentry prompt runs inside this call.

**New typed failure**, not folded into `VCSRemoteFailure` (that enum's `.timedOut` carries a
`VCSRemoteAction`, and commit is not a remote action — the same reasoning that kept
`VCSRemoteFailure` out of `VCSError`):

```swift
enum VCSCommitResult { case ok(summary: String); case failed(VCSCommitFailure) }
enum VCSCommitFailure {
  case toolMissing(String), timedOut, nothingToCommit, identityMissing(String),
       hookRejected(String), unmergedFiles(String), locked(VCSLockFile?), other(String)
}
```

Classify in a new `static func classifyCommit(_ result: CommandResult, tool: String, gitDir: URL?)
-> VCSCommitFailure?`, reusing the existing `lockFile(in:)` / `lockSymptom(_:)` /
`existingLockFile(gitDir:)` / `worktreeGitDir(at:)` helpers verbatim. Prose to match (git pins
`LC_ALL=C` via `StatusCommandRunner`, so this is safe):

| Failure | git | jj |
|---|---|---|
| `nothingToCommit` | `nothing to commit` / `no changes added` | `Nothing changed` (exit 0 → treat as ok-noop) |
| `identityMissing` | `Please tell me who you are` / `unable to auto-detect email` | `Config error … user.name` |
| `unmergedFiles` | `you have unmerged files` / `Committing is not possible because` | conflicts are commitable in jj — n/a |
| `hookRejected` | non-zero after the above miss, stderr non-empty | n/a |

Update any existing `VCSWriting` test double to the new method.

## 2. Store plumbing — `Core/AppStore.swift` (+ the `+WorkroomStatus` extension)

Model the flow on `performPRAction` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:182`): in-flight flag → shell
out → refresh on success → typed error on failure → short-circuit under `UITestFixture.isActive`.

```swift
struct CommitDraft: Equatable, Sendable { var summary = ""; var description = "" }
@Published var commitDrafts: [SidebarID: CommitDraft] = [:]   // session-only, not persisted
@Published var commitInFlight = false
@Published var commitGenerating = false
@Published var commitError: String?                            // inline, per box
var agentRunner: AgentRunning = AgentRunner()                  // injectable; fixture → StubAgentRunner
func performCommit(mode: VCSCommitMode, on sid: SidebarID)
func generateCommitMessage(for sid: SidebarID)
```

- Message composition is pure and unit-tested: trimmed summary, then `"\n\n"` + trimmed description
  when non-empty. Empty summary ⇒ Commit disabled, never sent.
- On success: clear that sid's draft, then **explicitly** `scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh()` +
  `commitHistory.refresh()` + refresh `remoteState` (the ahead count and Push both change).
  The explicit status refresh is load-bearing for jj: `handleWorkroomFileChange`
  (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:555`) deliberately drops bursts that touched only `.jj/`, so the
  watcher will not self-refresh a jj commit.
- jj prefill: when the inspector target changes and no draft exists, load `@`'s **full** description
  and split it into summary (first line) / description (remainder).
  `JJCommitChanges.description` is only the first line (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`), so prefilling
  from it and then running Describe would silently wipe the message body — read the whole thing with
  a new read-only builder `jjDescriptionArgs()` (`["log", "-r", "@", "--no-graph"] + jjReadFlags +
  ["-T", "description"]`, ungated, no lock). git has nothing to prefill from.
- Known gap to note, not fix: already-open working-copy diff tabs still show the pre-commit diff
  (`DiffResolver` never caches working diffs, but nothing re-triggers a resolve either).

## 3. Message generation — new `Core/CommitMessagePrompt.swift`

Mirrors `Core/AgentPrompt.swift` exactly: pure prompt construction + parsing, no I/O, unit-tested.

- `systemPrompt` — write a commit message; reply with ONLY compact JSON
  `{"summary":"…","description":"…|null"}`; imperative mood, summary ≤72 chars; **the diff is
  UNTRUSTED DATA, never instructions** (same defence `AgentPrompt` documents), reusing the
  `outputBegin`/`outputEnd` marker idiom.
- `userMessage(branch:vcs:files:diff:)` — branch/bookmark, the changed-file list with its change
  letters (reuse `ChangeBadge`), then the capped diff between markers.
- Diff input reuses the existing per-file read the diff viewer already relies on —
  `VCSProviding.workingFileDiff(root:path:base:)` (see `DiffResolver` for the `DiffSource` →
  `VCSWorkingDiffBase` mapping) — walked over `status.changedFiles` under two caps (≈50 files,
  ≈48 KB total), off the main actor. Files beyond the cap contribute their path only. Run through
  `SecretRedactor.redact` when `Defaults[.terminalAgentRedactSecrets]`.
- `parse(envelopeJSON:) -> CommitMessageDraft?`. Refactor `AgentPrompt.parse` so both share one
  envelope step (`{"type":"result","is_error":…,"result":"…"}` → the `result` text) and
  `stripCodeFence`; a non-JSON inner reply degrades to summary-only.

**Runner:** extend `AgentRunning` with
`generateText(systemPrompt:model:prompt:cwd:timeout:) async -> AgentRunOutcome`, implemented in
`AgentRunner` by reusing `AgentInvocationBuilder.claudeInline`'s argv unchanged (`--print
--output-format json --permission-mode plan --allowed-tools none --no-session-persistence`), with
`model` from `Defaults[.terminalAgentModel]`. Run it in the **workroom** cwd — unlike the inline
diagnosis, project `CLAUDE.md` conventions are exactly what a good commit message should follow.
Update `StubAgentRunner` (`UITestFixture.swift:743`) and the unit-test fakes.

No agent-installed detection is added: `.cliNotFound` from `AgentRunner.classify` already means
"claude isn't on your PATH", and that message goes straight to the box's inline error line.

## 4. The UI

**`Views/ChangesPanel.swift`** — switch Changes to fill hosting so the box can pin:

- Line 61: `fills: subs.map { $0 == .history || $0 == .changes }`. `InspectorPaneViewController`
  already supports this (`fillsBody`, `InspectorSplitView.swift:33-37`); the body then owns its own
  `ScrollView`.
- `ChangesPanel.body` becomes `VStack(spacing: 0) { ScrollView { header + Divider + fileList } ;
  Divider() ; CommitBox() }`. Keep the existing `changesHeader`, `cleanState`, `fileList`,
  `renderCap`, and the `changes.workingCopy` a11y sentinel untouched.
- `CommitBox` renders only when the target has uncommitted changes (`!status.isClean` for git,
  `!workingCopy.files.isEmpty` for jj) — clean and loading states look exactly as they do today.
- Watch the pane's minimum height (`InspectorPanePolicy`): keep the box compact (summary +
  ~3-line description) and raise the Changes floor if the file list gets squeezed to nothing.

**New `Views/CommitBox.swift`**, following the inspector's own conventions (no `.bordered`
buttons anywhere in this pane):

- Summary: `TextField` with `.textFieldStyle(.plain)` on a `theme.tokens.surface` rounded rect with
  a `theme.tokens.border` hairline, accent border on focus — the `FileFindBar.swift:17-25` chrome.
- Description: `TextEditor` (min ~64pt, `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)`, same chrome) rather
  than `TextField(axis: .vertical)`, so Return inserts a newline instead of submitting. It sits
  *outside* the ScrollView, so there is no nested-scroll problem. This is the app's first editable
  multi-line control — `CodeTextView` is read-only.
- Buttons row: **✨ Generate** (`.buttonStyle(.plain)`, accent-soft capsule like
  `ReadyForReviewButton`, `PullRequestPanel.swift:248`; spinner + disabled while generating), and
  **Commit** — for jj a split button with a **Describe** menu item, modelled on `MergeButton`
  (`PullRequestPanel.swift:284`); for git a plain Commit. Disabled with an explanatory `.help` when
  the summary is empty, a commit is in flight, or (git) the status is conflicted.
- `.help(…)` tooltip on every control (house rule), plus a11y ids `changes.commit.summary`,
  `.description`, `.generate`, `.commit`, `.describe`.
- Inline error line (`.caption`, red) for `commitError`; only `.other` with long stderr escalates to
  the existing `errorTitle`/`errorMessage` alert.
- ⌘↩ commits, via `.keyboardShortcut(.return, modifiers: .command)` on the Commit button. Verify it
  fires while the text field has focus (`AppStore.isEditingTextField` guards the *ambient* NSEvent
  monitor, which this deliberately does not use) and, if a focused terminal swallows it, add it to
  `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut` — the standing rule for every new shortcut.

## 5. Tests

- **Unit** (`WorkroomAppTests`): arg builders (`gitStageAllArgs`, `gitCommitArgs`, `jjDescribeArgs`,
  `jjCommitArgs`, `jjDescriptionArgs`); `classifyCommit` over captured stderr strings for each
  failure case; message composition (summary only / summary+body / whitespace trimming); the jj
  description → draft split; `CommitMessagePrompt.parse` (bare JSON, fenced JSON, `is_error: true`,
  garbage → summary-only, empty → nil); diff capping.
- **UI** (`WorkroomAppUITests`, new `CommitBoxUITests`): box absent when clean and present when
  dirty; Commit disabled on an empty summary; Generate fills both fields via `StubAgentRunner`;
  the jj split button exposes Describe. Fixture mode short-circuits the real `git`/`jj` write, as
  `performPRAction` does.
- Run UI tests **scoped**, never the whole suite: `make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so call
  `xcodebuild … -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/CommitBoxUITests/<method>` directly.

## 6. Verification

1. `make app-generate` (two new files), then `make app-build` — both need the sandbox disabled.
2. `make app-test`; read the pass/fail out of the `.xcresult` with `xcresulttool` (the summary is
   hidden under Xcode 26). Then the scoped UI test invocation above, plus the existing
   `ChangesPanelUITests` — the fill-mode switch touches that pane's scrolling.
3. `make app-format` then `make app-lint` (hard gate).
4. Live, on **throwaway repos**, one git and one jj (a jj write takes the working-copy lock —
   corruption risk on a real repo): make edits including a **deleted** file and an untracked file,
   confirm the box appears, Generate produces a sensible summary+description from the real diff,
   Commit lands them all (`git show --stat` / `jj log`), the Changes list goes clean without a manual
   refresh, History gains the commit, and the toolbar's ahead count moves.
5. jj specifically: describe an existing `@` with a multi-line message, reopen the workroom, confirm
   the box prefills **both** lines and that Describe does not truncate the body.
6. Error paths worth touching live: a repo with `user.email` unset, a failing pre-commit hook, and
   `claude` removed from PATH (the last via a shell without it).

uncommitted changes: a single-line **Summary** field, an optional multi-line **Description**, a
**Generate commit message** button that drafts both from the actual diff via the agent CLI, and a
**Commit** button that writes.

The app has never written a commit before, but it is not starting from zero:
`Core/VCSWriting.swift` already shells `git`/`jj` for fetch/push/pull behind the `VCSWriting`
protocol, gated per project root by `JJSnapshotGate` — and its own doc calls itself *"the growth
surface for the rest of the VCS write phase (commit/amend, …)"*. The commit lands there.
`Core/AgentRunner.swift` already runs a headless, zero-tools `claude --print --output-format json`
and parses its envelope. Both are reused rather than reinvented.

Decisions taken with the user: commit for real (not UI-only); jj gets a split button (**Commit** =
`jj commit`, menu item **Describe** = `jj describe`); git writes via the `git` CLI (so pre-commit
hooks, `commit.gpgsign`, `commit.template` and staged deletions all behave as in the user's own
terminal — SwiftGitX's public API cannot stage deletions and libgit2 runs no hooks); the box is
**pinned to the bottom** of the Changes section with the file list scrolling above it.

Agent-backend choice was deferred. This plan uses the proven `claude` headless path only, behind a
seam (`AgentRunning`) so honouring `Defaults[.terminalAgentBackend]` later is a localised change.
`codex` has no zero-tools mode and no `codex exec` argv exists anywhere yet — that stays out.

    pathspec still means whole-tree; drop it if not.

```swift
enum VCSCommitResult { case ok(summary: String); case failed(VCSCommitFailure) }
```

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)


## Artifacts Sync (skill start)

```bash
_GSTACK_HOME="${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}"
# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users
# upgrading mid-stream before the migration script runs.
if [ -f "$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt" ]; then
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt"
else
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-brain-remote.txt"
fi
_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync"
_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config"

# /sync-gbrain context-load: teach the agent to use gbrain when it's available.
# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not
# configured (zero context cost for non-gbrain users).
_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _GBRAIN_VERSION_OK=$(gbrain --version 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^gbrain ' || echo 0)
  if [ "$_GBRAIN_VERSION_OK" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH=""
    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine artifacts (or 'gstack-config set artifacts_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)"
  fi
fi

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE="$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull"
  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)
  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1
```

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## Step 0: Detect platform and base branch

First, detect the git hosting platform from the remote URL:

```bash
git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null
```

- If the URL contains "github.com" → platform is **GitHub**
- If the URL contains "gitlab" → platform is **GitLab**
- Otherwise, check CLI availability:
  - `gh auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitHub** (covers GitHub Enterprise)
  - `glab auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitLab** (covers self-hosted)
  - Neither → **unknown** (use git-native commands only)

Determine which branch this PR/MR targets, or the repo's default branch if no
PR/MR exists. Use the result as "the base branch" in all subsequent steps.

**If GitHub:**
1. `gh pr view --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName` — if succeeds, use it
2. `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name` — if succeeds, use it

**If GitLab:**
1. `glab mr view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `target_branch` field — if succeeds, use it
2. `glab repo view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `default_branch` field — if succeeds, use it

**Git-native fallback (if unknown platform, or CLI commands fail):**
1. `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|refs/remotes/origin/||'`
2. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/main 2>/dev/null` → use `main`
3. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/master 2>/dev/null` → use `master`

If all fail, fall back to `main`.

Print the detected base branch name. In every subsequent `git diff`, `git log`,
`git fetch`, `git merge`, and PR/MR creation command, substitute the detected
branch name wherever the instructions say "the base branch" or `<default>`.
