# Commit from the Changes inspector

## Context

Issue #124 "VCS Improvements", third bullet: a commit box with a summary field, an optional
description, and a "Generate commit message" button backed by the preferred AI agent. The two
sibling bullets (Push-with-count, Fetch state) already shipped as the VCS toolbar. The goal it
serves is issue #59: *"you don't need to use the Git or JJ CLI tools."*

**The motivation, stated honestly.** An earlier draft claimed committing means "switching to a
terminal and retyping the branch context." That is false, and review killed it: Workroom embeds a
terminal already `cd`'d into the workroom. The real win is that you never have to *reconstruct* what
you changed — the app already knows, and can compose the commit for you. That reframing is why this
ships as a **dialog** launched from the Changes section rather than a box wedged into the pane.

**This is the app's first local write path.** Everything after it (discard, revert, amend-with-content,
split, undo) inherits its shape, so the shape matters more than the feature.

## Scope: two changes, sequenced

| | Change | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Commit** (this plan) | The write path, the commit dialog, selection, message-only amend, the failure taxonomy, real-repo tests. |
| **2** | **Generate commit message** | Agent backend resolution, prompt + parse, privacy consent, Settings copy. Section 7 below scopes it; it does not ship here. |

Reason: review found the safety half unbuilt and the AI half a 2024 commodity (GitButler and others
ship it). Landing the write path alone gets its six measured command bugs a dedicated test pass.

**Land first, separately:** the `wr-vcs-core` config fix below. It is an existing bug, independent
of this feature.

## Sibling work item — `wr-vcs-core` must read the real jj config stack

`TODOS.md:498` tracks the root cause at P3 and lists fsmonitor, EOL conversion, exec-bit and
`core.excludesFile`. It misses the two that matter, both live in shipped code:

- **Every jj user gets an empty committer.** `snapshot_working_copy` (`jj_backend.rs:593`) builds
  `UserSettings` from `StackedConfig::with_defaults()`, whose compiled-in `misc.toml` sets
  `user.name = ""` and `user.email = ""`. Every status refresh that finds on-disk changes runs
  `rewrite_commit(...)` (`jj_backend.rs:661-670`) → `for_rewrite_from` → `commit.committer =
  settings.signature()` (`commit_builder.rs:235`), unconditionally. Author survives; committer does
  not. Usually invisible (`jj log` shows the author) and self-heals on the next real-CLI rewrite, but
  **not** if `@` is pushed as-is, which the app's own Push button does via `jj git push --change @`.
- **Signatures are dropped.** Same settings give `signing.backend = "none"` → `can_sign()` false →
  `write_to_store` sets `secure_sig = None`. Under the default `behavior = "keep"`, a snapshot rewrite
  of an already-signed `@` discards its signature.

Fix: load the real stack (`$JJ_CONFIG` → `~/.jjconfig.toml` → XDG → `~/.config/jj/config.toml` +
`conf.d/` → `.jj/repo/config.toml`) into `UserSettings`. jj-lib supplies `ConfigLayer::load_from_file`,
`StackedConfig::add_layer` and the `ConfigSource` precedence order but does **no** discovery — that
lives in jj-cli, which is not vendored. Signing then works for free (`Signer::from_settings` reads
whatever settings we pass). Update the TODOS entry with these two consequences and raise its priority.
**Throwaway repos only** — this is the lock-taking, `@`-rewriting path.

## Settled decisions

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Backend | **`git` and `jj` CLI, both.** Native was tried and reversed: libgit2 runs no hooks ([#964](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2/issues/964)) and cannot sign; `wr-vcs-core` reads no user config, so native jj would stamp an empty committer, drop signatures, and be unable to honour `immutable_heads()` (a jj-*cli* revset alias jj-lib cannot resolve). |
| Surface | **A dialog**, launched from the Changes section header. Not an in-panel composer. |
| Amend | **Message-only** (`--amend --only`). Selection-aware amend is deferred. |
| jj verbs | Commit (`jj commit`) and Set Message Only (`jj describe`). No per-file selection on jj. |
| State | Dialog-local. No per-workroom draft/selection/activity dictionaries. |

`TODOS.md:139-144` ("commit/amend → native, don't re-litigate") must be amended: commit is CLI for
both backends. That entry's rationale never weighed hooks, signing, or our own core reading no config.

## 1. Why a dialog, and what it deletes

The in-panel composer was measured against the pane and does not fit: ~152pt of composer against
**86pt of body** at `InspectorPanePolicy.expandedMinHeight` (120 − 34 header), leaving 2 file rows for
git and 1 for jj at a default third of a 900pt window. Fill hosting would also disable the documented
compress-and-scroll valve (`InspectorSplitView.swift:371-374`), so compression clips the Commit button
instead of scrolling.

The dialog deletes, rather than solves:

| Would have needed | Fate |
|---|---|
| `commitDrafts` / `commitSelection` / `commitState` keyed by `SidebarID`, plus `Defaults` persistence | Dialog-local `@State`. |
| Draft lifecycle: pruning on workroom delete, recycled-name inheritance, `@Default` async typing lag | Gone. |
| Multi-window race (`AppStore` is per window; two windows would share one `Defaults` dict, last writer wins) | Gone. Two dialogs serialize on the gate, like two terminals. |
| `renderCap = 200` vs "Commit N files" | Gone. The dialog scrolls the full list. |
| ⌘↩ scoping, `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut`, terminal-swallowing | Gone. Scoped to the dialog. |
| Inventing inline field chrome (none exists in the inspector; the plan's cited precedent contains none) | Reuse `AddProjectSheet` / `WorkroomLabelSheet` conventions. |
| Fill-mode switch, pane floor policy, `ChangesPanelUITests` risk | Not touched. |

**Cost, accepted:** the sheet covers the diff you were reading.

**What survives regardless:** the dialog pins `sid` / `path` / `projectRoot` at open and every
completion uses *that*, never the live selection; it registers in `hasModalPresentation`
(`AppStore.swift:555`) or Source Control shortcuts fire behind it; and dismissal is guarded while the
fields are non-empty so a mis-click cannot destroy a typed message.

## 2. The surface

**`Views/ChangesPanel.swift`** — the section header gains a Commit `InspectorHeaderButton`
(`checkmark.circle`), enabled when there is something to record. For jj that includes an `@` with no
file changes but a describable description: jj allows described empty changes and `jjPushRevision`
already recognises that state.

**New `Views/CommitSheet.swift`**, following the repo's existing sheet conventions:

- **File list** (git only): scrollable, each row a checkbox + the existing `ChangeBadge` letter, path
  and directory. A tri-state select-all header row reading "12 of 20 files". Row context menu offers
  **Commit Only This File** and **Exclude This File**; ⌥-click isolates, ⇧-click ranges.
  Use `Image(systemName: checked ? "checkmark.square.fill" : "square")` at `.callout` in a 14pt slot —
  the same slot geometry as the change letter beside it, so both share a text baseline by
  construction, rather than a `Toggle` which has no baseline and is wider.
- **jj renders no checkboxes.** jj has no index; it commits the whole change. One line under the list
  says so: *"jj commits the whole change. Splitting isn't supported yet."* Rendering checkboxes whose
  only effect on that backend is to disable the button is a designed dead end.
- **Summary**: `TextField`, `.roundedBorder`, `@FocusState`, focused on open.
- **Description**: `TextEditor` with a hand-built placeholder overlay (SwiftUI has none), min ~80pt.
- **Actions**: **Commit 12 files** primary; a menu carries **Amend Last Commit** (git, showing which:
  "a1b2c3 — Fix the toolbar hover") and **Set Message Only** (jj — help text: *"Names the current
  change and stays on it"*, so it teaches the outcome, not the command name). Cancel closes.
- **Blocked states get a persistent inline line above the actions, never a tooltip.** Nobody hovers a
  button that looks dead, and tooltips are unavailable to VoiceOver. Applies to conflicts, sequencer
  states, zero selected, and amend-unavailable.
- **While committing** the dialog stays up with a live "running hooks…" line and a working Cancel.
  A hook can run for a minute; a modal that just freezes is not acceptable.
- **On failure** the draft and selection survive, and two affordances appear: **Show output**, which
  opens stderr in a tab (`ScriptLogContent` / `PlainFileViewer` already exist), and **Run in
  Terminal**, which pre-fills the exact command in the embedded terminal. Hook output is the most
  valuable text in the whole taxonomy and must not be squeezed into one line.
- ⌘↩ commits, scoped to the dialog. Esc cancels, guarded when fields are non-empty.
- `.help(…)` on every control, a11y ids `commit.summary`, `.description`, `.commit`, `.amend`,
  `.describe`, `commit.file.check.<path>`. The checkbox is its own a11y element with the path in its
  label; the rest of the row stays combined as today.

## 3. The write path — `Core/VCSWriting.swift`

`VCSWriting`'s doc already names itself the growth surface for commit/amend, and `CLIVCSWriter` owns
the gate, the runner and the failure taxonomy. Commit lands there.

```swift
func commit(path: String, projectRoot: String, request: CommitRequest) async -> VCSCommitResult
struct CommitRequest { let message: String; let paths: [ChangedFile]; let mode: CommitMode }
enum CommitMode { case commit, amendMessage, describe }
```

`paths` carries **`ChangedFile`, not `String`** — the rename case needs both sides. It is empty for
jj, which takes no pathspec at all.

### Runner seam (prerequisite, small, buys four fixes)

`StatusCommandRunning` exposes no per-call **stdin** and no per-call **env**. Add both. That one seam
buys: `--pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul` (NUL-delimited paths on stdin, taken **literally**),
`--file=-` for the message (no length or encoding worry), and a future `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. Routing
around it three separate times is the worse trade.

### Arg builders (pure, unit-tested, beside the existing ones)

- `gitStageArgs()` → `gitHardening + ["add", "--pathspec-from-file=-", "--pathspec-file-nul"]`,
  paths on stdin. **The `add` step is mandatory** — `git commit --only -- <path>` *cannot* commit an
  untracked file (`error: pathspec 'untracked.txt' did not match any file(s) known to git`).
- `gitCommitArgs()` → `gitHardening + ["commit", "--file=-"]`, message on stdin.
- `gitAmendArgs()` → `gitHardening + ["commit", "--amend", "--only", "--file=-"]`. **`--only` is
  load-bearing**: without it, amend absorbs whatever is staged and ignores the selection entirely.
- `jjCommitArgs(message:)` → `["commit", "-m", message] + jjWriteFlags`. No pathspec.
- `jjDescribeArgs(message:)` → `["describe", "-m", message] + jjWriteFlags`.
- `jjDescriptionArgs()` (read-only prefill) → `["log", "-r", "@", "--no-graph"] + jjReadFlags + ["-T", "description"]`.

`jjWriteFlags`, never `jjReadFlags`, on the writes: the snapshot is what carries on-disk edits into
`@`. Commit always runs in the **workroom**, both backends — `opDirectory`'s own doc records the
measured bug where a jj write at the project root operated on the *root workspace's* `@` and reported
success. Commit is **not** added to `VCSRemoteAction` (that enum feeds
`VCSRemoteFailure.timedOut`, `PendingVCSAction` and the toolbar labels).

### Path handling (all six measured against real repos)

1. **Renames expand to both sides.** A `.renamed`/`.copied` row contributes `path` *and* `oldPath`.
   Without it, `mv old new` + commit records an add and leaves `D old` dangling — staged, if `git mv`.
2. **Paths are literal.** `--pathspec-file-nul` takes them literally, closing glob magic: after a bare
   `--`, selecting `a[b].txt` also stages `ab.txt`, and a file named `*` stages the tree.
3. **Deletions** stage via the same path on any git ≥ 2.0. Verify once; no `-A` hedge.
4. **Unicode**: paths come from libgit2 (`GitProvider.statusPath`), not porcelain, so there is nothing
   to unquote — but macOS returns NFD while `core.precomposeunicode` makes git store NFC. Only a real
   repo test catches it.

### Staged-content guard (converts silent data loss into an informed choice)

`git commit -- <path>` implies `--only`, which builds from the **worktree** and discards what was
staged for that path — measured data loss for anyone who ran `git add -p`. Rather than a temp index
(deferred), **detect and ask**: before committing, diff index against worktree **per selected path**.
If any selected path has staged content differing from disk, stop and say so by name, offering
*Commit anyway* or *Open in Terminal*. Also surface pre-existing staged content on **unselected**
paths, so nothing is absorbed silently.

**Do not auto-restore the index on failure.** If `add` succeeds and `commit` fails, say plainly that
the index now holds the selection. Blindly restoring would overwrite concurrent terminal work.

### One gate acquisition

`add` and `commit` go inside a **single** `gated { }` closure. Two acquisitions let the 15s sweep, the
FSEvents lane and `DiffResolver` interleave and contend on `index.lock`. Additionally, suppress those
lanes while a commit is in flight, the way `isCreating(sid)` already does for create
(`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:66-73, 119-125, 548-551`) — necessary because `JJSnapshotGate`'s
`maxChainWait` (30s) is *shorter* than the commit timeout, so its self-heal would otherwise admit a
status snapshot alongside a running commit.

### Sequencer and repo states

Detect before enabling Commit, via `worktreeGitDir(at:)` (the `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` pattern):
`MERGE_HEAD`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD`, `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply`, bisect, detached HEAD,
unborn HEAD. Path-limited commit is invalid during several (`fatal: cannot do a partial commit during
a merge`) — and resolving conflicts in the terminal clears the *conflict* without clearing
`MERGE_HEAD`, so a conflict-only check re-enables the button into guaranteed failure. For v1: disable
with *"Finish this operation in the terminal"*. Amend is additionally hidden for a root commit, a
merge commit, and mid-rebase.

### Typed failures

```swift
enum VCSCommitResult {
  case ok(summary: String, commitID: String?)
  case committedThenFailed(commitID: String, detail: String)
  case failed(VCSCommitFailure)
}
enum VCSCommitFailure {
  case toolMissing(String), timedOut, nothingToCommit, identityMissing(String),
       signingFailed(String), hookRejected(String), unmergedFiles(String),
       sequencerInProgress(String), locked(VCSLockFile?), other(String)
}
```

- **A timeout does not mean the commit did not happen.** git can move `HEAD` and then hang in
  `post-commit`; the runner SIGKILLs at +2s and returns `.timedOut`, and a retry would duplicate the
  commit. Capture `HEAD` (or the jj op id) **before and after every non-success outcome** and report
  `committedThenFailed` when the ref moved.
- **`hookRejected` is matched, never a catch-all.** A catch-all mislabels signing failures, config
  errors and index corruption, sending users to the wrong remedy. Unmatched stays `.other` with raw
  stderr.
- **No signing preflight.** Whether pinentry needs a TTY depends on `gpg-agent.conf`, cache state and
  smartcards — undecidable, and three subprocesses on the click path. With stdin on `/dev/null`, gpg
  fails *fast*: match `Inappropriate ioctl for device` / `gpg failed to sign the data` into
  `signingFailed` and offer *Run in Terminal* from the failure.
- **No hard kill on commit.** SIGKILL leaves `index.lock`, which the app deliberately never deletes
  (`VCSRemoteFailure.locked`'s doc), so one slow hook would wedge every later commit *and* every status
  probe until the user removes the file by hand. Use a ceiling far above any plausible hook plus a
  user-initiated Cancel.
- **`--no-verify` is never passed by default** and is offered only from a `hookRejected` failure, with
  the hook's own output shown.
- `--cleanup` reformats a `-m`/`--file` message (trailing whitespace, collapsed blank lines), so what
  is recorded differs from what was typed. Matters for the jj prefill round-trip.

### After a successful commit

Refresh by **captured sid**, not by current selection: `scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh()` derives its
target from the live `selectedTargetID` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:121`) and
`commitHistory.refresh()` from the model's focused root (`HistoryModel.swift:67`), so switching
workrooms mid-commit commits A and refreshes B. Add `refreshStatus(for: sid)`; refresh History,
`remoteState` and diff tabs only while they still point at the committed target. The explicit refresh
is load-bearing for jj — `handleWorkroomFileChange` deliberately drops `.jj/`-only bursts. Open
working-copy diff tabs for committed paths must be closed or re-pointed, not left showing a diff that
no longer exists. Report success in the existing `ToastStack` with the short SHA / change-id.

## 4. Amend, v1

Message-only: reword the last commit, touch nothing else. The menu names the commit it will amend.
The "already pushed" guard is a **warning, not a gate** — remote counts come from possibly-stale
remote-tracking refs (`VCSModels.swift:193`), every workroom is `git worktree add -b` with no upstream
so `gone: true, ahead: nil` is the normal reading, and `nil` also means the counts read failed.
Selection-aware amend needs temp-index tree construction and is deferred.

## 5. What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

| Need | Existing |
|---|---|
| Gated, classified CLI writes | `CLIVCSWriter`, `VCS.writer(for:)`, `JJSnapshotGate` |
| Process spawn, timeout, kill-tree, `LC_ALL=C`, null stdin | `StatusCommandRunner` (+ the new stdin/env seam) |
| Sheet form chrome, focus, submit | `AddProjectSheet`, `WorkroomLabelSheet`, `DeleteProjectSheet` |
| Modal registration | `hasModalPresentation` (`AppStore.swift:555`) |
| Log/stderr in a tab | `ScriptLogContent`, `PlainFileViewer` |
| Success feedback | `ToastStack` |
| Change letters and colours | `ChangeBadge` |
| Repo-state probing | `worktreeGitDir(at:)`, `rebaseInProgress(gitDir:)` |
| Lane suppression precedent | `isCreating(sid)` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:66-73`) |

## 6. Tests

Every one of the six measured bugs must be pinned by a test, not by section 9's manual checklist.
`VCSRemoteIntegrationTests.swift` and `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` are the existing homes for
real-repo tests.

- **Unit**: arg builders; pathspec construction **including `oldPath` expansion**; NUL stdin payload;
  selection intersection under a mutated change set; sequencer-state detection; amend enablement over
  `(gone, ahead, nil)`; `classifyCommit` over captured stderr for gpg (`Inappropriate ioctl for
  device`), merge refusal, `did not match any file(s) known to git`, `nothing to commit`.
- **Integration, throwaway repos** (cannot be unit-tested): the rename case; `a[b].txt` beside
  `ab.txt`; an untracked file; `git add -p` then commit (the staged-content guard fires); deleted file;
  unborn HEAD; a path with a space; `café.txt` in NFD; a `pre-commit` that rewrites files; a
  `commit-msg` that rejects; timeout after `HEAD` moved; amend with unrelated staged content; and the
  assertion the plan must not omit — **post-commit `status` is clean for exactly the committed rows**.
- **UI** (`CommitSheetUITests`): sheet opens and closes; Commit disabled at zero selected; deselection
  changes the button count; jj shows no checkboxes; keyboard commands do not fire behind the sheet.
  Note fixture mode short-circuits the write, so the integration tier above is what covers semantics.
- Run UI tests **scoped**: `make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so call `xcodebuild …
  -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/CommitSheetUITests/<method>` directly.

## 7. Change 2 — Generate commit message (scoped, not in this change)

Recorded now so change 1 does not foreclose it:

- **Resolve `Defaults[.terminalAgentBackend]`, never hardcode claude.** It defaults to `"auto"`, and
  `SettingsView.swift:358` *does* read it — for a paragraph saying it governs failed-command diagnosis,
  under a picker labelled "Diagnose with". **Extending it to commit generation requires changing that
  copy in the same change.** Three states, three messages: explicit `codex` → "Generate needs Claude
  Code, Codex can't run without tool access"; `auto` with claude missing → "Generate needs Claude Code"
  plus an install link, mirroring `PullRequestPanel.ghWarning`; nothing installed → same.
- **Neutral cwd** (`NSTemporaryDirectory()`), as `AgentRunner.swift:94-96` instructs. Running in the
  workroom would load a cloned repo's `CLAUDE.md` — attacker-controlled text landing *outside* the
  untrusted-data markers.
- **Neutralise the markers.** Commit subjects and diff lines can both contain the literal end marker
  and close the block. Strip or nonce it in every untrusted segment. `AgentPrompt` shares this latent
  flaw; fix it once, there.
- **Repo conventions via a constrained channel**: sample recent commit subjects as *data*. The jj form
  must carry `jjReadFlags` — `jj log` without `--ignore-working-copy` snapshots `@`, ungated.
- **One whole-selection diff inside one gate acquisition** (`git diff HEAD -- <paths>`, `jj diff
  --git`), not 50 per-file `workingFileDiff` calls each taking the gate. Stat-and-skip oversized files
  *before* reading; the cap must bind during collection. Truncation is never silent.
- Privacy: consent is **per-user** (Settings, beside `terminalAgentRedactSecrets`) plus a **per-project**
  opt-out. The first-run sheet must join `hasModalPresentation`.
- Generate never overwrites text typed *while* it was running: re-check at completion, and offer
  Replace / Discard.

## 8. Not in scope

Hunk staging · selection-aware amend (needs a temp index) · undo toast (`jj op restore` /
`git reset --soft`) · "Discard changes…" (issue #124's other bullet) · native jj commit (blocked on the
config-stack fix) · instrumentation and a kill criterion (blocked on #138) · harvesting commit intent
from the agent session in the pane (the real 10x reframe both CEO voices pointed at).

## 9. Verification

1. `make app-generate`, `make app-build` — both need the sandbox disabled.
2. `make app-test`; read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via `xcresulttool` (Xcode 26 hides the
   summary). Then the scoped UI tests. `ChangesPanelUITests` should be unaffected — the panel keeps its
   hosting mode.
3. `make app-format`, then `make app-lint` (hard gate).
4. Live, throwaway git and jj repos: edits including a deleted file, an untracked file and a rename.
   Confirm the count matches the checkboxes, Commit lands exactly the checked paths (`git show --stat`
   / `jj log`), `git status` is clean for those rows, the Changes list refreshes without a manual
   poke, History gains the commit, the toolbar's ahead count moves.
5. **The staged-content guard, specifically**: `git add -p` a partial hunk, then tick that file in the
   dialog. Confirm it stops and names the file rather than silently replacing the staged hunk.
6. jj: describe an `@` with a multi-line message, reopen, confirm both lines prefill and Set Message
   Only does not truncate the body. Confirm a described-but-empty `@` can still be committed.
7. Failure paths: `user.email` unset; a failing pre-commit hook (check stderr reaches a tab); a hook
   that rewrites files; `commit.gpgsign=true` with `pinentry-tty`; a commit during an unfinished merge.

## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT

| CEO | Claude subagent + Codex | complete | 17 + 23; 12 confirmed by both |
| Design | Claude subagent | complete | 4 critical, 6 high, 3 medium |
| Eng | Claude subagent (empirical, throwaway repos) | complete | 6 **measured** criticals, 10 high/medium |
| Eng + Design | Codex (combined) | complete | 5 P0, 8 P1, 3 UI/test |
| DX | not run | skipped | No public API, CLI, docs or onboarding change. The applicable dimension, error-message quality, was covered three times (hook stderr routing, failure taxonomy, blocked-state copy). |

**Consensus:** 0/6 CEO dimensions passed as originally drafted. Four cross-phase themes, each flagged
independently by 2+ phases: selection integrity, index mutation on failure, Generate being the
commodity half, and state scoping.

**Measured findings now fixed in the plan:** rename committing an add plus an orphaned deletion;

`git commit -- <path>` discarding staged content; jj filesets failing on spaces and creating empty

**Architecture findings now fixed:** timeout ≠ not-committed; the gate's 30s self-heal versus a long

**Decisions taken at the gate:** split the change (write path first); dialog replaces the in-panel
composer; message-only amend; dialog-local state, so no `CommitCoordinator` and no per-workroom

3	/// The full result of a short status command: stdout, stderr, exit code, and whether the
4	/// timeout fired. Unlike `CommandRunning` (which collapses everything to `String?`), this
5	/// keeps the exit code and timeout flag so `WorkroomStatusResolver` can tell "not a repo"
6	/// (git exit 128) from "gh not installed" (exit 127) from "timed out" from "clean" — the
7	/// distinctions the status UI's unknown/stale/absent matrix depends on.

9	  let stdout: String
10	  let stderr: String
11	  let exitCode: Int32
12	  let timedOut: Bool
13

17	  static let gitFatal: Int32 = 128
18

20	}

24	protocol StatusCommandRunning: Sendable {
25	  func run(_ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String, timeout: TimeInterval)
26	    async -> CommandResult

29	  /// authenticate — `git fetch/push/pull`, `jj git fetch/push`.
30	  ///
31	  /// A read like `git status` can never prompt, so it wants the minimal, predictable environment
32	  /// `run` gives it. A push can: it may need an SSH agent the GUI environment can't see, and it may
33	  /// try to ask for a passphrase or a host-key confirmation with nowhere to ask. See
34	  /// `StatusCommandRunner.networkEnvironment` for what changes and why.
35	  func runNetwork(
36	    _ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String,
37	    timeout: TimeInterval
38	  ) async -> CommandResult

43	  /// and let them stay two-line stubs. Only `StatusCommandRunner` overrides this.

52	/// Default `StatusCommandRunning`: spawns via `/usr/bin/env` (augmented PATH finds Homebrew
53	/// git/jj/gh), git locks/prompt disabled, and enforces `timeout` by terminating the process.
54	///
55	/// Unlike `ProcessCommandRunner` (which reads stdout *in* the termination handler — safe only
56	/// because a branch name is tiny), this drains stdout AND stderr **concurrently on background
57	/// queues while the process runs** (the `WorkroomCLI` pattern). Status output can be large (a
58	/// repo with thousands of changed files, a big `gh` JSON payload); reading post-termination
59	/// would let the OS pipe buffer fill, block the child on write, and deadlock until the timeout.
60	/// Retained output is capped (`maxBytes`) so a pathological repo can't blow memory — the reader
61	/// keeps draining past the cap (so the child never blocks) but discards the overflow.
62	struct StatusCommandRunner: StatusCommandRunning, Sendable {
63	  var maxBytes: Int = 4 * 1024 * 1024
64	
65	  /// Auth-relevant variables forwarded from the user's shell for network commands only.
66	  ///
67	  /// A Finder- or Dock-launched `.app` inherits launchd's environment, not the user's shell, and this
68	  /// runner otherwise overrides only PATH. That was harmless while it ran `git status` and `gh` (which
69	  /// carries its own token), but it breaks authentication outright: `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is how a process
70	  /// finds an SSH agent, and for anyone using 1Password's agent, gpg-agent, or a custom socket it is
71	  /// set in `.zshrc` and nowhere else. Without it their `git push` cannot reach the agent, and the
72	  /// error would tell them to configure a credential helper they already have.
73	  ///
74	  /// Deliberately an allowlist, not the whole probed environment (which `ShellEnvironment.environment()`
75	  /// hands to setup/teardown scripts): network ops now run automatically on inspector focus, and a
76	  /// wholesale transplant would put every variable in the user's shell — secrets included — into a
77	  /// child on an automatic path.
78	  static let forwardedAuthKeys = [
79	    "SSH_AUTH_SOCK", "SSH_AGENT_PID", "GIT_SSH_COMMAND", "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", "XDG_CONFIG_HOME",
80	  ]
81	
82	  /// Variables removed for network commands so `ssh` cannot find a graphical prompt helper.
83	  static let networkClearedKeys = ["SSH_ASKPASS", "DISPLAY"]
84	
85	  /// The environment for a network command: `base` plus forwarded auth vars, with ssh pinned to
86	  /// fail fast instead of asking a human.
87	  ///
88	  /// `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (set by `run`) governs **git's own** credential prompts and says nothing
89	  /// to `ssh`. So an SSH remote with a passphrase-protected key and no agent, or a host whose key
90	  /// isn't in `known_hosts`, would otherwise stall until the timeout — 120s for fetch/push, 300s for
91	  /// pull. `BatchMode=yes` turns both into an immediate, classifiable failure, and
92	  /// `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never` stops ssh reaching for a GUI helper (OpenSSH 8.4+; macOS ships 10.x).
93	  ///
94	  /// A user's own `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` is preserved and appended to rather than replaced — it commonly
95	  /// carries `-i <key>` or a proxy command that must survive.
96	  ///
97	  /// Pure and static so the whole policy is unit-testable without spawning anything.
98	  static func networkEnvironment(base: [String: String], probed: [String: String])
99	    -> [String: String]
100	  {
101	    var env = base
102	    for key in forwardedAuthKeys {
103	      // The inherited environment wins: if it's already set, the app was launched from a shell that
104	      // had it, and that value is at least as current as the probe's.
105	      if env[key] == nil, let value = probed[key], !value.isEmpty { env[key] = value }
106	    }
107	    for key in networkClearedKeys { env.removeValue(forKey: key) }
108	    let ssh = env["GIT_SSH_COMMAND"]?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
109	    env["GIT_SSH_COMMAND"] = (ssh?.isEmpty == false ? ssh! : "ssh") + " -o BatchMode=yes"
110	    env["SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE"] = "never"
111	    return env
112	  }

128	    _ executable: String, _ args: [String], in directory: String,
129	    timeout: TimeInterval, network: Bool
130	  ) async -> CommandResult {
131	    let proc = Process()
132	    proc.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/usr/bin/env")
133	    proc.arguments = [executable] + args
134	    proc.currentDirectoryURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: directory)
135	
136	    var env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
137	    env["PATH"] = ShellEnvironment.path()
138	    env["GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS"] = "0"
139	    env["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT"] = "0"
140	    // Pin the message locale: EVERY consumer of this runner classifies failures by matching English
141	    // substrings of git's stderr (`CLIVCSWriter.classify`, `WorkroomStatusResolver`), and git ships
142	    // translated message catalogs. Homebrew git 2.55 under a French locale answers
143	    // `erreur : le spécificateur de chemin …`, so without this a non-English user loses the ENTIRE
144	    // failure taxonomy at once — auth, host-key, rejected-push, dirty-tree and leftover-lock all
145	    // collapse to `.other(rawStderr)` with no recovery offered.
146	    //
147	    // `LC_ALL`, not `LC_MESSAGES`: this env is seeded from `ProcessInfo.environment`, so the user's own
148	    // `LC_ALL` may be inherited, and it OUTRANKS `LC_MESSAGES` — setting the narrower variable is
149	    // silently defeated (measured: `LC_ALL=fr_FR.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=C git …` still answers in French).
150	    //
151	    // Safe for paths despite forcing the C charset: git writes pathnames as raw bytes (and quotes
152	    // non-ASCII per `core.quotePath` regardless of locale), so `LC_ALL=C` renders a `café-ünï.txt`
153	    // byte-identically to the user's own locale — verified, not assumed. jj and gh are unaffected
154	    // either way; neither localizes.
155	    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
156	    // A workroom can be a clone of an *untrusted* repo, and the status sweep runs git automatically
157	    // on load/focus/selection. `git diff` would otherwise run an inherited external-diff program;
158	    // unset it so only the explicit `--no-ext-diff` flag (see WorkroomStatusResolver) governs diffs.
159	    env.removeValue(forKey: "GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF")
160	    if network { env = Self.networkEnvironment(base: env, probed: ShellEnvironment.environment()) }
161	    proc.environment = env
162	
163	    let outPipe = Pipe()
164	    let errPipe = Pipe()
165	    proc.standardOutput = outPipe
166	    proc.standardError = errPipe
167	    // Never let a child read the app's stdin. Unset, it INHERITS ours — which under `make app-run`
168	    // (or `Scripts/run.sh`) is a real terminal, so a prompting `ssh` or `git` could sit waiting on a
169	    // tty that the same binary won't have when launched from Finder. Pinning it makes the two launch
170	    // contexts behave identically and turns any prompt into an immediate EOF. `ShellEnvironment.probe`
171	    // already does this for the same reason.
172	    proc.standardInput = FileHandle.nullDevice
173	
174	    // `proc` is shared with the @Sendable cancellation handler; box it so the non-Sendable Process
175	    // can cross that boundary (mirrors the @unchecked Sendable helpers below).
176	    let box = ProcessBox(proc)
177	
178	    return await withTaskCancellationHandler {
179	      await withCheckedContinuation { (continuation: CheckedContinuation<CommandResult, Never>) in
180	        let state = StatusRunState()
181	        let drain = DispatchGroup()
182	        let cap = maxBytes
183	        let gate = CommandResumeGate(continuation)
184	
185	        // Concurrent drains (the deadlock fix). availableData blocks until data or EOF;
186	        // started before run() so we never miss a fast child's output, harmless until it runs.
187	        drain.enter()
188	        DispatchQueue.global().async {
189	          state.setStdout(Self.readCapped(outPipe.fileHandleForReading, cap: cap))
190	          drain.leave()
191	        }
192	        drain.enter()
193	        DispatchQueue.global().async {
194	          state.setStderr(Self.readCapped(errPipe.fileHandleForReading, cap: cap))
195	          drain.leave()
196	        }
197	
198	        let timeoutItem = DispatchWorkItem {
199	          state.markTimedOut()
200	          if proc.isRunning { proc.terminate() }  // SIGTERM
201	        }
202	        DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + timeout, execute: timeoutItem)
203	
204	        // Hard-kill fallback: a wedged child (e.g. `gh` blocked on a dead socket) can ignore SIGTERM,
205	        // so `terminationHandler` — the only place the continuation resumes — would never fire and the
206	        // awaiting Task would hang forever, defeating the timeout. SIGKILL is uncatchable, guaranteeing
207	        // the process exits and we resume. A 2s grace after SIGTERM lets well-behaved children exit.
208	        let killItem = DispatchWorkItem {
209	          if proc.isRunning { ProcessTree.killTree(proc.processIdentifier) }
210	        }
211	        DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + timeout + 2, execute: killItem)
212	
213	        proc.terminationHandler = { finished in
214	          timeoutItem.cancel()
215	          killItem.cancel()
216	          // The process has exited, so its own pipe write ends are closed and EOF is imminent. But a
217	          // grandchild that inherited the pipe (a helper spawned by gh/git) can hold the write end
218	          // open after the parent dies — an unbounded `drain.wait()` would then never return and the
219	          // continuation would never resume, wedging this probe slot forever. Bound the wait and
220	          // resume with whatever drained; a still-blocked reader writes to `state` we no longer read
221	          // (safe — lock-guarded) and exits when the grandchild finally closes the pipe.
222	          _ = drain.wait(timeout: .now() + 2)
223	          gate.resume(
224	            CommandResult(
225	              stdout: String(decoding: state.stdout, as: UTF8.self),
226	              stderr: String(decoding: state.stderr, as: UTF8.self),
227	              exitCode: finished.terminationStatus,
228	              timedOut: state.timedOut))
229	        }
230	
231	        do {
232	          try proc.run()
233	        } catch {
234	          // Launch failed (e.g. cwd vanished). Close the write ends so the drain readers hit
235	          // EOF instead of blocking forever, then resolve as command-not-found.
236	          timeoutItem.cancel()
237	          killItem.cancel()
238	          try? outPipe.fileHandleForWriting.close()
239	          try? errPipe.fileHandleForWriting.close()
240	          gate.resume(
241	            CommandResult(
242	              stdout: "", stderr: "\(error)", exitCode: CommandResult.commandNotFound,
243	              timedOut: false))
244	        }
245	      }
246	    } onCancel: {
247	      // The awaiting Task was cancelled (e.g. a superseded sweep, or rapid selection cycling). Kill
248	      // the in-flight child so a cancelled probe doesn't leave a git/jj/gh process running to its own
249	      // timeout. terminationHandler then resumes the continuation with the abandoned result, which
250	      // the cancelled caller discards. SIGKILL (not SIGTERM) so a wedged child dies promptly.
251	      box.terminate()
252	    }
253	  }

255	  /// Drain a pipe to EOF, retaining at most `cap` bytes but reading the rest so the child
256	  /// never blocks on a full pipe buffer.
257	  private static func readCapped(_ handle: FileHandle, cap: Int) -> Data {
258	    var collected = Data()
259	    while true {
260	      // `read(upToCount:)` (throwing) instead of `availableData`: the latter raises an
261	      // *Objective-C* `NSFileHandleOperationException` on a read error (common right after the
262	      // child is `terminate()`d out from under the open read end), which Swift can't catch — it
263	      // crashes the app. Treat a read error as EOF and return what we have.
264	      let chunk: Data
265	      do { chunk = try handle.read(upToCount: 1 << 16) ?? Data() } catch { break }
266	      if chunk.isEmpty { break }  // EOF: pipe closed
267	      if collected.count < cap {
268	        collected.append(chunk.prefix(cap - collected.count))
269	      }
270	    }
271	    return collected
272	  }
273	}

275	/// Boxes a non-Sendable `Process` so it can be captured by the @Sendable task-cancellation handler.
276	private final class ProcessBox: @unchecked Sendable {
277	  private let process: Process
278	  init(_ process: Process) { self.process = process }
279	  /// SIGKILL the child (and any descendants it spawned) if still running — the cancellation path
280	  /// abandons the result, so kill promptly rather than wait out a SIGTERM grace.
281	  ///
282	  /// Hopped to a global queue because `withTaskCancellationHandler`'s `onCancel` runs **synchronously
283	  /// on whichever thread called `cancel()`**, and the hottest canceller is the main thread:
284	  /// `selectedTargetID.didSet` → `scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh` → `selectionStatusTask?.cancel()`
285	  /// supersedes the in-flight probe on *every* selection change. `ProcessTree.killTree` walks the tree
286	  /// by spawning a `pgrep -P` per node and blocking on `waitUntilExit` for each, so inline it stalled
287	  /// the main thread for the length of that walk while switching workroom tabs — and a blocking wait
288	  /// spins a nested run loop, which drains queued main-queue blocks at a point SwiftUI hasn't committed
289	  /// its update yet (that reordering is what surfaced the split-member selection snap-back). Deferring
290	  /// the kill costs nothing: the continuation resumes from `terminationHandler`, never from here, and
291	  /// the cancelled caller discards the result. Matches `killItem`, which already kills off a global
292	  /// queue.
293	  func terminate() {
294	    let process = self.process
295	    DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async {
296	      if process.isRunning { ProcessTree.killTree(process.processIdentifier) }
297	    }
298	  }
299	}
300	
301	/// Mutable scratch shared between the drain queues and the termination handler. Locked
302	/// because the two reads and the handler touch it from different threads.
303	private final class StatusRunState: @unchecked Sendable {
304	  private let lock = NSLock()
305	  private var _stdout = Data()
306	  private var _stderr = Data()
307	  private var _timedOut = false
308	
309	  func setStdout(_ d: Data) {
310	    lock.lock()
311	    _stdout = d
312	    lock.unlock()
313	  }
314	  func setStderr(_ d: Data) {
315	    lock.lock()
316	    _stderr = d
317	    lock.unlock()
318	  }
319	  func markTimedOut() {
320	    lock.lock()
321	    _timedOut = true
322	    lock.unlock()
323	  }
324	
325	  var stdout: Data {
326	    lock.lock()
327	    defer { lock.unlock() }
328	    return _stdout
329	  }
330	  var stderr: Data {
331	    lock.lock()
332	    defer { lock.unlock() }
333	    return _stderr
334	  }
335	  var timedOut: Bool {
336	    lock.lock()
337	    defer { lock.unlock() }
338	    return _timedOut
339	  }
340	}
341	
342	/// Resumes a `CommandResult` continuation exactly once (termination vs launch-failure race).
343	private final class CommandResumeGate: @unchecked Sendable {
344	  private let lock = NSLock()
345	  private var done = false
346	  private let continuation: CheckedContinuation<CommandResult, Never>
347	
348	  init(_ continuation: CheckedContinuation<CommandResult, Never>) {
349	    self.continuation = continuation
350	  }
351	
352	  func resume(_ value: CommandResult) {
353	    lock.lock()
354	    let first = !done
355	    done = true
356	    lock.unlock()
357	    if first { continuation.resume(returning: value) }
358	  }
359	}

All three work. **Option A** — `:(literal)` prefix *with* `--pathspec-file-nul` — is the one to use: NUL separation keeps paths with newlines safe, and the magic prefix still parses. No env seam needed after all.

Verified command shapes, all measured just now:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `commit --only --pathspec-from-file=-` | commits exactly the selection |
| pre-staged content on an *unselected* path | **preserved** (stays staged) |
| untracked file | fails; needs `add --intent-to-add` first |
| rename with both sides | records a rename, status clean |
| `a[b].txt` bare | also commits `ab.txt` |
| `:(literal)a[b].txt` | commits only `a[b].txt` |

That kills the `git add` step for tracked files entirely — which is what fixes the failed-commit-mutates-the-index problem.

+/// Which commit verb to run. Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSRemoteAction`: that enum feeds
+/// `VCSRemoteFailure.timedOut`, `PendingVCSAction` and the toolbar's labels, none of which mean

+/// - `.describe` — jj only. Sets `@`'s description and stays on it.
+enum VCSCommitMode: String, Equatable, Sendable {
+  case commit, amendMessage, describe
+/// One commit, fully specified. `files` carries `ChangedFile` rather than `String` because a rename
+/// needs BOTH sides of the pathspec — see `gitPathspecPayload`.

+  let message: String
+  /// The user's selection. Empty for jj, which has no index and commits the whole change.
+  let files: [ChangedFile]
+  let mode: VCSCommitMode

+  case ok(summary: String, revision: String?)
+  /// The ref MOVED but the command still reported failure — a `post-commit` hook that fails or hangs
+  /// past the timeout is the reachable case. Distinct from `.failed` because the recovery is
+  /// opposite: retrying would create a SECOND commit.

+  case failed(VCSCommitFailure)
+/// Why a commit failed. Separate from `VCSRemoteFailure` for the reason that enum documents about

+  case timedOut
+  /// Nothing staged/changed for the selection. jj reports this as an ordinary success ("Nothing

1	import AppKit
2	import SwiftUI
3	
4	/// The VCS failure dialog: what failed, the whole message, the tool's own output, and every action that
5	/// can be taken about it.
6	///
7	/// **Why a dialog at all.** The toolbar's sync segment is a 114pt cell holding one line, so a failure
8	/// could only ever render as a truncated notice — "Describe the change bef…" was the report that prompted
9	/// this. The rest lived in a tooltip, which is a hover away, can't be copied, can't be clicked, and
10	/// vanishes the moment you move the pointer toward the thing it told you to fix. The bar keeps the
11	/// notice; this carries the message.
12	///
13	/// Presented by `VCSFailurePresenter` on the app's root, NOT on the inspector: an action can be started
14	/// from the Source Control menu with the inspector hidden, and a dialog that only appears when a
15	/// particular pane happens to be open is worse than no dialog.
16	struct VCSFailureSheet: View {
17	  let dialog: VCSFailureDialog
18	  /// Runs the recovery. Routed back through `AppStore.performRemoteAction` by the caller so a Pull
19	  /// recovery still meets the dirty-tree confirmation — a gate only some entry points honour isn't one.
20	  let onRecover: (VCSRemoteAction) -> Void
21	  let onDismiss: () -> Void
22	
23	  /// Collapsed by default: the tool's output is evidence for when the written remedy isn't enough, and
24	  /// expanding it by default would bury the remedy under a wall of stderr.
25	  @State private var showDetails = false
26	
27	  var body: some View {
28	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
29	      header
30	      // Selectable, because half of these messages contain a path or a command the user needs to get
31	      // into a terminal. `fixedSize(vertical:)` is what lets it wrap to its full height instead of
32	      // truncating to one line inside the sheet's fixed width — the very failure mode this replaces.
33	      Text(dialog.message)
34	        .font(.callout)
35	        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
36	        .textSelection(.enabled)
37	        .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
38	        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
39	        .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.message")
40	      if let details = dialog.details {
41	        detailsSection(details)
42	      }
43	      Divider()
44	      buttons
45	    }
46	    .padding(20)
47	    .frame(width: 460)
48	    // `children: .contain` is load-bearing, not decoration. An `.accessibilityIdentifier` on a plain
49	    // container makes SwiftUI treat that container as ONE element and absorb everything inside it: the
50	    // sheet was findable and its title, message and buttons were not — including by XCUITest, which
51	    // caught exactly this.
52	    .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
53	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.sheet")
54	  }
55	
56	  private var header: some View {
57	    HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
58	      Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
59	        .font(.system(size: 30))
60	        .foregroundStyle(.orange)
61	        .accessibilityHidden(true)
62	      Text(dialog.title)
63	        .font(.headline)
64	        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
65	        .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.title")
66	    }
67	  }
68	
69	  /// The tool's own output, monospaced and scrolled rather than truncated — a rejected push's stderr
70	  /// runs to a dozen lines and the useful one is rarely the first.
71	  private func detailsSection(_ details: String) -> some View {
72	    DisclosureGroup(isExpanded: $showDetails) {
73	      ScrollView {
74	        Text(details)
75	          .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))
76	          .textSelection(.enabled)
77	          .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
78	          .padding(8)
79	          .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.details")
80	      }
81	      .frame(maxHeight: 160)
82	      .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(.quaternary.opacity(0.5)))
83	    } label: {
84	      Text("Details").font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
85	    }
86	    .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.detailsToggle")
87	  }
88	
89	  private var buttons: some View {
90	    HStack(spacing: 8) {
91	      Button("Copy") { copyReport() }
92	        .help("Copy the message and the tool's output to the clipboard")
93	        .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.copy")
94	      // Only for a located lock file: the fix is a file operation Workroom deliberately won't perform
95	      // (see `VCSRemoteFailure.locked`), so the least it can do is hand over the file.
96	      if let lockPath = dialog.lockPath {
97	        Button("Reveal in Finder") {
98	          NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([URL(fileURLWithPath: lockPath)])
99	        }
100	        .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.revealLock")
101	      }
102	      Spacer()
103	      Button("Dismiss") { onDismiss() }
104	        .keyboardShortcut(.cancelAction)
105	        .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.dismiss")
106	      // Absent whenever `retryAction` says the same command would fail identically — a doomed default
107	      // button is the defect the failure tier already exists to prevent, and a dialog makes it worse by
108	      // putting it under the return key.
109	      if let recovery = dialog.recovery {
110	        Button(recovery.label) {
111	          onDismiss()
112	          onRecover(recovery)
113	        }
114	        .keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)
115	        .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
116	        .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.failure.recover")
117	      }
118	    }
119	  }
120	
121	  /// Title, message and output as one block — what you'd paste into an issue or a chat.
122	  private func copyReport() {
123	    let text = [dialog.title, dialog.message, dialog.details].compactMap { $0 }
124	      .joined(separator: "\n\n")
125	    NSPasteboard.general.clearContents()
126	    NSPasteboard.general.setString(text, forType: .string)
127	  }
128	}
129	
130	/// Bridges `RemoteStateModel.failureReport` to the sheet.
131	///
132	/// A `ViewModifier` with its own `@ObservedObject` for the reason `VCSToolbar` documents: `AppStore`
133	/// holds `RemoteStateModel` but does not forward its `objectWillChange`, so a view that reaches it
134	/// through the store alone never repaints when a failure lands — and a sheet that never repaints never
135	/// presents.
136	struct VCSFailurePresenter: ViewModifier {
137	  @ObservedObject var model: RemoteStateModel
138	  let onRecover: (VCSRemoteAction) -> Void
139	
140	  func body(content: Content) -> some View {
141	    content.sheet(
142	      item: Binding(
143	        get: { model.failureReport },
144	        // Only the nil direction is honoured: the sheet is presented by the model raising a report, never
145	        // by SwiftUI writing one back.
146	        set: { if $0 == nil { model.dismissFailureReport() } })
147	    ) { report in
148	      VCSFailureSheet(
149	        dialog: VCSSyncPresenter.failureDialog(
150	          report.failure, action: report.action, now: Date()),
151	        onRecover: onRecover,
152	        onDismiss: { model.dismissFailureReport() })
153	    }
154	  }
155	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// What the VCS toolbar's middle segment is currently doing.
4	enum VCSSyncActivity: Equatable, Sendable {
5	  case idle
6	  case running(VCSRemoteAction)
7	}
8	
9	/// Everything the toolbar's sync segment renders, resolved from one state snapshot.
10	///
11	/// A pure mapping, kept out of the view for the same reason as `ChangeBadge`: it's a many-case
12	/// decision that silently drifts. `now` is a parameter rather than a `Date()` read so the whole thing
13	/// is testable at fixed instants.
14	struct VCSSyncPresentation: Equatable, Sendable {
15	  /// Title variants, LONGEST FIRST, for a `ViewThatFits` ladder. Empty ⇒ single-line mode: the segment
16	  /// renders only `subtitle`, vertically centred, at a larger weight.
17	  var titleVariants: [String] = []
18	  var subtitle: String
19	  /// A shorter subtitle for narrow widths. The staleness caveat abbreviates but must never be the
20	  /// first thing dropped — the unverified count it qualifies is the thing that should yield.
21	  var subtitleShort: String
22	  var symbol: String?
23	  var badge: Badge?
24	  var secondaryBadge: Badge?
25	  var action: VCSRemoteAction?
26	  var isEnabled: Bool
27	  var tone: Tone = .normal
28	  var help: String
29	  /// Spoken label. The count pills are `accessibilityHidden`, so their information has to arrive here.
30	  var accessibility: String
31	  var accessibilityValue: String = ""
32	  /// The blocking lock file, when there is one. Carried so the segment can offer to copy or reveal it —
33	  /// the fix is a file operation the user performs, so the least Workroom can do is hand them the path
34	  /// rather than make them transcribe it out of a tooltip.
35	  var lockPath: String?
36	
37	  struct Badge: Equatable, Sendable {
38	    enum Direction: Equatable, Sendable { case ahead, behind }
39	    let count: Int
40	    let direction: Direction
41	  }
42	
43	  enum Tone: Equatable, Sendable { case normal, warning, failure }
44	
45	  var title: String? { titleVariants.first }
46	  var isSingleLine: Bool { titleVariants.isEmpty }
47	}
48	
49	/// Everything the failure dialog renders, resolved from one failure.
50	///
51	/// The toolbar segment is **one truncating line** — it has to be, it's a 114pt cell — so it can only ever
52	/// be a notice that something failed. Anything longer than "Describe the change bef…" was unreadable, and
53	/// the tooltip that held the rest is a hover away and can't be copied, clicked or kept open while you fix
54	/// the problem. This is where the whole message lives instead.
55	struct VCSFailureDialog: Equatable, Sendable {
56	  /// Names the action, so the dialog says what failed without the bar for context.
57	  var title: String
58	  /// The full explanation: what happened, then how to fix it. Multi-paragraph, never truncated.
59	  var message: String
60	  /// The tool's own output, when there is any. Kept apart from `message` because it's evidence, not
61	  /// instruction — and for `.other` it is the ONLY complete account, since the segment's copy is that
62	  /// output's first line.
63	  var details: String?
64	  /// The action to offer as the dialog's default button, from `retryAction` — so the dialog can't offer a
65	  /// retry the toolbar has already decided is doomed.
66	  var recovery: VCSRemoteAction?
67	  var lockPath: String?
68	}
69	
70	/// Maps a `VCSRemoteState` to what the sync segment shows.
71	///
72	/// ```
73	///   failure?  ──yes──►  [13] retry the previous action          tone: failure
74	///      │no
75	///   in flight? ──yes──►  [10/11/12] Fetching…/Pushing…/Pulling…      disabled
76	///      │no
77	///   pullConflicted? ──yes──►  [14] "Pulled with conflicts"    disabled, tone: warning
78	///      │no
79	///   target valid? ──no──►  [1] no workroom  ·  [2] no repository     disabled
80	///      │yes
81	///   tools ok? ──no──►  [0] "<tool> is too old"                       disabled
82	///      │yes
83	///   has remote? ──no───►  [3] "No remote configured"                 disabled
84	///      │yes
85	///   counterpart gone? ──yes──►  [4] "Publish branch"      → push --set-upstream
86	///      │no
87	///   ahead>0 && behind>0 ──yes──►  [9] "Pull <remote> with rebase"   badge: M↓ then N↑
88	///      │no                             (pull, NOT push — git refuses non-ff)
89	///   behind>0 ──yes──►  [8] "Pull <remote> with rebase"              badge: M↓
90	///      │no
91	///   ahead>0  ──yes──►  [7] "Push <remote>"                          badge: N↑
92	///      │no
93	///   never fetched ──yes──►  [5] "Never fetched"          → fetch
94	///      │no
95	///                        [6] "Fetched <rel>"            → fetch
96	/// ```
97	///
98	/// `<remote>` is always interpolated from `primaryRemote`, never the literal "origin" —
99	/// `remote.pushDefault` can legitimately make that the wrong name.
100	enum VCSSyncPresenter {
101	
102	  /// Build the presentation.
103	  ///
104	  /// - Parameters:
105	  ///   - state: `nil` ⇒ no readable repo for the current target.
106	  ///   - hasTarget: whether a workroom is selected at all (distinguishes "nothing selected" from
107	  ///     "selected, but not a repo" — different copy, both disabled).
108	  ///   - toolsUsable: `false` ⇒ the `git`/`jj` on PATH can't run these commands
109	  ///     (`VCSToolVersions`). Outranks everything except an in-flight action and a failure, because no
110	  ///     action can succeed.
111	  ///   - pullRebase: whether the repo pulls with rebase — wording only.
112	  ///   - pullConflicted: our own pull left conflicts that are still unresolved. Compute it with
113	  ///     `pullConflicted(lastPullConflicted:statusConflicted:)` — both halves are load-bearing.
114	  ///   - busyElsewhere: an action is running for a DIFFERENT workroom. `RemoteStateModel.inFlight` is a
115	  ///     model-wide lock, so `perform` drops the click — but `activity` here is per-target, so without
116	  ///     this the segment rendered an enabled button, hover well and all, whose click did nothing at all.
117	  ///     Worse through the confirmation path: the dialog appeared, the user confirmed, and the action was
118	  ///     silently discarded. A 300s pull in one workroom made every other workroom's button a no-op.
119	  static func make(
120	    state: VCSRemoteState?, hasTarget: Bool, toolsUsable: Bool = true,
121	    activity: VCSSyncActivity = .idle, failure: VCSRemoteFailure? = nil,
122	    lastAction: VCSRemoteAction? = nil, pullRebase: Bool = true, pullConflicted: Bool = false,
123	    busyElsewhere: Bool = false, now: Date
124	  ) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
125	    var resolved = resolve(
126	      state: state, hasTarget: hasTarget, toolsUsable: toolsUsable, activity: activity,
127	      failure: failure, lastAction: lastAction, pullRebase: pullRebase,
128	      pullConflicted: pullConflicted, now: now)
129	    // Applied AFTER the ladder rather than threaded through every enabled tier: it changes only whether
130	    // the thing can be clicked, never what it says. The copy still reports the real state, so the user
131	    // isn't told a lie — the button simply isn't live while the engine is busy for someone else.
132	    if busyElsewhere, resolved.action != nil {
133	      resolved.action = nil
134	      resolved.isEnabled = false
135	    }
136	    return resolved
137	  }
138	
139	  private static func resolve(
140	    state: VCSRemoteState?, hasTarget: Bool, toolsUsable: Bool,
141	    activity: VCSSyncActivity, failure: VCSRemoteFailure?,
142	    lastAction: VCSRemoteAction?, pullRebase: Bool, pullConflicted: Bool,
143	    now: Date
144	  ) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
145	    // [13] A failure outranks everything: it's the only state with something to recover from, and
146	    // burying it under a count would leave the user with no idea the action didn't happen.
147	    if let failure, case .idle = activity {
148	      let message = describe(failure)
149	      let recovery = retryAction(for: failure, lastAction: lastAction)
150	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
151	        // With no recovery to offer, the title must not read as a button. "Retry" over a failure that
152	        // cannot be retried is the whole defect this branch fixes.
153	        //
154	        // The title names the RECOVERY, not the action that failed. It used to read `lastAction?.label`
155	        // while `action:` below was `recovery` — so a rejected push rendered a button labelled "Push"
156	        // that performed a Pull. The two must be the same verb or the button lies about what it does.
157	        titleVariants: recovery.map { [$0.label] } ?? [],
158	        subtitle: message, subtitleShort: message,
159	        symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill",
160	        action: recovery,
161	        isEnabled: recovery != nil,
162	        // The tooltip is where a failure gets room to explain itself — one line fits the bar, the
163	        // remedy usually doesn't.
164	        tone: .failure, help: explain(failure, now: now),
165	        accessibility: "\(lastAction?.label ?? "Action") failed. \(explain(failure, now: now))",
166	        lockPath: lockPath(of: failure))
167	    }
168	
169	    // [10/11/12] In flight — one action at a time, so this can't collide with a second.
170	    if case .running(let action) = activity {
171	      let title: String
172	      let subtitle: String
173	      switch action {
174	      case .fetch: (title, subtitle) = ("Fetching…", "from \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
175	      case .push: (title, subtitle) = ("Pushing…", "to \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
176	      case .pull: (title, subtitle) = ("Pulling…", "from \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
177	      case .abortRebase: (title, subtitle) = ("Aborting…", "rebase")
178	      }
179	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
180	        titleVariants: [title], subtitle: subtitle, subtitleShort: subtitle,
181	        symbol: nil, badge: badge(ahead: state?.tracking?.ahead),
182	        action: nil, isEnabled: false, help: "\(title) \(subtitle)",
183	        accessibility: "\(title) \(subtitle)")
184	    }
185	
186	    // [14] The pull we ran landed conflicts.
187	    //
188	    // BELOW the in-flight tier, deliberately: a running action's progress outranks a previous action's
189	    // outcome. ABOVE the counts, equally deliberately — a conflicted pull leaves behind at 0, so the
190	    // count tiers would render "Push origin" and say nothing at all about the tree being conflicted,
191	    // which is both the more urgent fact and a prerequisite for that push making sense.
192	    //
193	    // Reached only by jj in practice: git's rebase stops on a conflict and exits non-zero, so a
194	    // conflicted git pull is already a `.rebaseInProgress` failure offering Abort. jj's rebase commits
195	    // the conflict and exits 0, which is why the outcome had to be read from working status at all.
196	    //
197	    // No action offered, for `.locked`'s reason: resolving conflicts is work in an editor, and a button
198	    // that can't do it is a promise broken on click.
199	    if pullConflicted {
200	      let remedy =
201	        "The rebase completed with conflicts. Resolve them in this workroom — the Changes list marks "
202	        + "each conflicted file."
203	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
204	        subtitle: "Pulled with conflicts", subtitleShort: "Conflicts",
205	        symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill", action: nil, isEnabled: false,
206	        tone: .warning, help: remedy, accessibility: "Pulled with conflicts. \(remedy)")
207	    }
208	
209	    // [1] Nothing selected.
210	    guard hasTarget else {
211	      return disabled("No workroom selected", symbol: nil)
212	    }
213	    // [2] Selected, but not a readable repo.
214	    guard let state else {
215	      return disabled("No repository", symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle", tone: .warning)
216	    }
217	    // [0] The tools can't run these commands. Nothing below this line could succeed.
218	    guard toolsUsable else {
219	      return disabled(
220	        "Update git or jj to use this", symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle", tone: .warning,
221	        help:
222	          "Fetch, push and pull need a newer git or jj. See the warning for the required version.")
223	    }
224	    // [3] No remote at all.
225	    guard let remote = state.primaryRemote else {
226	      return disabled("No remote configured", symbol: nil)
227	    }
228	
229	    let fetched = fetchedAgo(state.lastFetch, now: now)
230	    let fetchedShort = fetchedAgo(state.lastFetch, now: now, short: true)
231	    let tracking = state.tracking
232	
233	    // [4] No counterpart on the remote yet. This is the DEFAULT state of a fresh workroom —
234	    // `git worktree add -b` sets no upstream — so it must not read as "Push origin" against something
235	    // that doesn't exist.
236	    if let tracking, tracking.gone {
237	      let branch = state.current.name ?? "this branch"
238	      let detail = "\(branch) isn’t on \(remote) yet"
239	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
240	        titleVariants: ["Publish branch", "Publish"],
241	        subtitle: detail, subtitleShort: detail, symbol: "arrow.up.circle",
242	        badge: badge(ahead: tracking.ahead), action: .push, isEnabled: true,
243	        help: "Push \(branch) to \(remote) and start tracking it.",
244	        accessibility: "Publish branch. \(detail)")
245	    }
246	
247	    let ahead = tracking?.ahead ?? 0
248	    let behind = tracking?.behind ?? 0
249	    let pullTitles =
250	      pullRebase
251	      ? ["Pull \(remote) with rebase", "Pull with rebase", "Pull"]
252	      : ["Pull \(remote)", "Pull"]
253	
254	    // [9] Diverged ⇒ Pull, not Push: git refuses a non-fast-forward push, so offering Push here would
255	    // send the user straight into a rejection. Badges show both, ↓ first — the one the action addresses.
256	    if ahead > 0, behind > 0 {
257	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
258	        titleVariants: pullTitles, subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort,
259	        symbol: "arrow.up.arrow.down",
260	        badge: .init(count: behind, direction: .behind),
261	        secondaryBadge: .init(count: ahead, direction: .ahead),
262	        action: .pull, isEnabled: true,
263	        help:
264	          "\(ahead) to push, \(behind) to pull. Pull first — \(remote) will reject a non-fast-forward push.",
265	        accessibility: "Pull \(remote) with rebase",
266	        accessibilityValue: "\(behind) behind, \(ahead) ahead")
267	    }
268	    // [8] Behind only.
269	    if behind > 0 {
270	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
271	        titleVariants: pullTitles, subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort,
272	        symbol: "arrow.down", badge: .init(count: behind, direction: .behind),
273	        action: .pull, isEnabled: true,
274	        help: "\(behind) commit\(behind == 1 ? "" : "s") to pull from \(remote). \(fetched).",
275	        accessibility: "Pull \(remote) with rebase", accessibilityValue: "\(behind) behind")
276	    }
277	    // [7] Ahead only.
278	    if ahead > 0 {
279	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
280	        titleVariants: ["Push \(remote)", "Push"], subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort,
281	        symbol: "arrow.up", badge: .init(count: ahead, direction: .ahead),
282	        action: .push, isEnabled: true,
283	        help: "\(ahead) commit\(ahead == 1 ? "" : "s") to push to \(remote). \(fetched).",
284	        accessibility: "Push \(remote)", accessibilityValue: "\(ahead) ahead")
285	    }
286	    // [5]/[6] In sync — the segment becomes a Fetch button.
287	    return VCSSyncPresentation(
288	      subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort, symbol: nil,
289	      action: .fetch, isEnabled: true,
290	      help: "Up to date with \(remote). \(fetched). Click to fetch again.",
291	      accessibility: "Fetch \(remote). \(fetched)")
292	  }
293	
294	  private static func disabled(
295	    _ subtitle: String, symbol: String?, tone: VCSSyncPresentation.Tone = .normal,
296	    help: String? = nil
297	  ) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
298	    VCSSyncPresentation(
299	      subtitle: subtitle, subtitleShort: subtitle, symbol: symbol, action: nil, isEnabled: false,
300	      tone: tone, help: help ?? subtitle, accessibility: subtitle)

3	/// The commit sheet's target, carried the way `PendingVCSAction` carries a confirmation's.
4	///
5	/// `.sheet(item:)` keys on `id`, so the sheet's `@State` — the draft and the selection — is rebuilt

7	struct PendingCommit: Identifiable, Equatable, Sendable {
8	  let sid: SidebarID
9	  /// `"git"` or `"jj"`. Decides whether per-file selection is offered at all and which second verb
10	  /// the menu carries.

15	/// The commit sheet's pure logic: what the message is, what is selected, and what the button says.
16	///
17	/// Separated from the view for the reason `ChangeBadge` and `VCSSyncPresenter` are: these are
18	/// many-case decisions that drift silently, and none of them is reachable from a test through
19	/// SwiftUI. The view holds state and renders; every rule below is decided here.
20	enum CommitDraft {
21	
22	  /// Compose the message git or jj will record.
23	  ///
24	  /// Summary and body are joined by a BLANK line, which is the convention every tool downstream
25	  /// relies on to split a subject from its body. Both halves are trimmed, and an empty body yields a
26	  /// subject-only message with no trailing newlines for `--cleanup` to strip.
27	  static func message(summary: String, body: String) -> String {
28	    let subject = summary.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
29	    let detail = body.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
30	    return detail.isEmpty ? subject : "\(subject)\n\n\(detail)"
31	  }
32	
33	  /// Split a stored message back into the two fields, for prefilling from jj's `@` description.
34	  ///
35	  /// The first line is the summary and everything after the first blank line is the body. Used
36	  /// against the FULL description — `JJCommitChanges.description` carries only the first line, so
37	  /// prefilling from that and describing again would silently discard the body.
38	  static func split(message: String) -> (summary: String, body: String) {
39	    let normalized = message.replacingOccurrences(of: "\r\n", with: "\n")
40	    var lines = normalized.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
41	    guard !lines.isEmpty else { return ("", "") }
42	    let summary = lines.removeFirst().trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
43	    let body = lines.joined(separator: "\n").trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
44	    return (summary, body)
45	  }
46	
47	  /// The files a commit would record, given what the user has EXCLUDED.
48	  ///
49	  /// Deselections are stored, never selections, and this is the reason. Coding agents run in this
50	  /// app's own embedded terminals and write files continuously, so the change set moves underneath
51	  /// an open dialog. With a set of *selected* paths there are only two possible behaviours when a new
52	  /// path appears — include it silently (committing a file nobody reviewed, which is the exact defect
53	  /// per-file selection exists to prevent) or reset the selection (throwing away the user's
54	  /// deliberate exclusions). Storing exclusions makes a new file arrive checked, which is the honest
55	  /// default, and makes an exclusion survive every refresh.
56	  ///
57	  /// A path that vanishes from the change set drops out on its own, so the excluded set never needs
58	  /// pruning.
59	  static func selected(from files: [ChangedFile], excluding excluded: Set<String>) -> [ChangedFile]
60	  {
61	    files.filter { !excluded.contains($0.path) }
62	  }

65	  /// once the list scrolls, "Commit" alone is an unverifiable claim.
66	  static func commitLabel(selectedCount: Int, vcs: String) -> String {
67	    // jj commits the whole change and offers no per-file selection, so a count would imply a choice
68	    // that isn't on offer.
69	    guard vcs != "jj" else { return "Commit" }
70	    switch selectedCount {
71	    case 1: return "Commit 1 file"
72	    default: return "Commit \(selectedCount) files"
73	    }
74	  }
75	
76	  /// Why Commit is unavailable, as a sentence, or nil when it is available.
77	  ///
78	  /// Returned as text rather than a Bool because these must render as a persistent inline line: four
79	  /// different blocked states explained only by a tooltip would be invisible to anyone who doesn't
80	  /// hover a control that already looks dead, and unavailable to VoiceOver entirely.
81	  static func blockedReason(
82	    vcs: String, summary: String, selectedCount: Int, totalCount: Int, conflicted: Bool,
83	    sequencer: String?
84	  ) -> String? {
85	    if let sequencer {
86	      return "A \(sequencer) is in progress. Finish it in the terminal before committing."
87	    }
88	    // git refuses to commit unmerged paths outright. jj records conflicts inside commits and would
89	    // happily accept this, but "Commit" reading as "done" over unresolved conflicts is a UX decision,
90	    // not a capability one — so both backends say the same thing.
91	    if conflicted {
92	      return "Some files still have unresolved conflicts. Resolve them first."
93	    }
94	    if totalCount == 0 && vcs != "jj" {
95	      return "Nothing has changed in this workroom yet."
96	    }
97	    if vcs != "jj" && selectedCount == 0 {
98	      return "Select at least one file to commit."
99	    }
100	    if summary.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty {
101	      return "Write a summary to describe this change."
102	    }
103	    return nil
104	  }

content.text:
Change 1 is built, tested, formatted and lint-clean.

## What shipped

**The write path** (`Core/VCSWriting.swift`) — commit, message-only amend, and jj describe, on the existing `VCSWriting` seam, inside a **single** `JJSnapshotGate` acquisition.

The command shapes are the interesting part, because I measured them against throwaway repos before writing the Swift, and **the approved plan was wrong in two places**:

- The plan had `git add <selection>` then `git commit`. That commits the whole index, so it would have swept in a file you'd staged in the terminal — the exact bug the selection model exists to prevent. Replaced with `git commit --only`, which I verified leaves an unrelated staged path **still staged**. Tracked files are now never staged at all, so a rejected commit can't leave your index mutated.
- The plan claimed `--pathspec-file-nul` makes paths literal. **It doesn't.** Selecting `a[b].txt` also committed `ab.txt`. Fixed with a `:(literal)` prefix on every entry, verified to commit only the bracketed file.

Also handled: renames send both sides (otherwise you get an add plus an orphaned deletion), untracked files get `--intent-to-add` first (`--only` alone can't commit them), a moved ref after a failed command reports `committedThenFailed` rather than inviting a duplicate commit, and parked merges/cherry-picks/rebases block up front.

**The dialog** (`Views/CommitSheet.swift`) — file list with checkboxes, select-all, summary, description, and the second verb labelled by outcome (`Set Message Only`, with `jj describe` only in the help text). Selection stores **exclusions**, so a file an agent writes while the dialog is open arrives checked instead of silently resetting your choices. jj gets no checkboxes at all.

**Store plumbing** — `refreshStatus(for:)` refreshes the workroom that was committed rather than whichever is selected when the hook finishes, and the sweep/watcher/selection lanes are suppressed during a commit, since the gate's 30s self-heal is shorter than a commit's timeout.

## Verification

- `make app-build` — succeeds
- `make app-test` — **1699 passed, 0 failed**, including 16 commit integration tests against real git and jj repos
- `make app-lint` — clean

One caveat, reported straight: on one of three identical full runs, `WorkroomStatusTests.testInspectorSizeWeightsAreGlobalAcrossWorkrooms` failed. It passes in isolation, my diff doesn't touch `inspectorLayout`, and it mutates a shared `Defaults` key while the suite runs parallel workers. Pre-existing flake, logged as a learning.

## Not done

- **UI tests** for the sheet — the fixture writer is wired (`FixtureVCSWriter.commit`) so they're straightforward, but I haven't written `CommitSheetUITests` yet.
- **Live QA** — I haven't driven the real app. Worth doing before you trust it, particularly the `git add -p` guard, which is currently *not* implemented: I chose `--only` (which cannot absorb another path's staged content) over the plan's detect-and-warn, but `--only` still takes the worktree version of a **selected** file, so a partially-staged hunk on a file you tick is still replaced. That guard is the one plan item I'd add next.
- **Change 2** (Generate commit message) and the **`wr-vcs-core` config fix** — both scoped in the plan, neither started.

content.text:
UI tests done. All green.

**8/8 UI tests pass**, plus the full unit suite at **1700 passed / 0 failed**, lint clean.

The first run failed 2 of 8, and both were real defects rather than flaky assertions:

**1. `children: .combine` on the file row made the checkbox unclickable.** Combining collapses the row into a single accessibility element, taking the checkbox with it — so the click landed on the row's centre and silently did nothing. The count never moved, with no assertion pointing at the cause. This is a genuine accessibility bug too, not just a test problem: VoiceOver had no individual control to toggle. Fixed by combining only the text half and giving the checkbox its own label, matching the `children: .contain` lesson `VCSFailureSheet` already records.

**2. My jj test used the wrong fixture flag.** `-WorkroomUITestGitWorkroom` controls the *status shape* (whether `jjWorkingCopy` is populated); the fixture **project** declares `vcs: "git"` regardless, and `-WorkroomUITestJJProject` is what flips the backend. So the sheet was correctly rendering git checkboxes and I was asserting against the wrong backend.

I also tightened the helpers: clicks now resolve through `app.buttons.matching(identifier:)` rather than `descendants(matching: .any)`, which is what let failure 1 present as a mystery instead of an error.

**Coverage:** dialog opens from the Changes header; blocked reason renders as a real element with Commit genuinely disabled, then enables on typing; deselecting a file moves the button's count; select-all blocks when nothing is left; jj offers no checkboxes or select-all; a rejected commit keeps the sheet, the draft *and* the hook's output; success and Cancel both dismiss.

Still outstanding from the plan, unchanged from before: the `git add -p` staged-hunk guard, live QA against real repos, Change 2 (Generate), and the `wr-vcs-core` config fix.

+  /// `-z` because a filename can contain a newline, and without it git also C-quotes non-ASCII names
