content.text:
Verified the top claims against real repos and the code. This is not a clean review — there are real blockers.

**Confirmed by measurement:**

**1. A plain `mv` rename fails the entire commit.** `GitProvider` runs status with `.renamesWorkingTree` (`GitProvider.swift:279`), so `mv old new` arrives as one `.renamed` row whose new path git has never seen. `runCommitSequence` intent-adds only `.change == .untracked` (`VCSWriting.swift:1610`), so the new side is never registered. Measured just now:

```
error: pathspec ':(literal)new.txt' did not match any file(s) known to git   (exit 1)
```

Nothing is committed — including the unrelated `other.txt` ticked in the same selection. `classifyCommit` has no marker for it, so it lands in `.other` with no remedy. Every editor rename and every coding-agent rename hits this; only `git mv` escapes, which is exactly what my integration test used.

**2. A successful commit can be reported as "Committed, but something afterwards failed."** `VCSWriting.swift:1097` builds `err = stderr + stdout` and line 1100 matches the nothing-to-commit markers *before* the `result.ok` guard at 1102. git echoes the subject on stdout, so `-m "explain the nothing to commit error"` classifies a clean exit-0 commit as `.nothingToCommit`; the ref moved, so it becomes `.committedThenFailed`. Four agents found this independently.

**3. Retry after a failed commit skips the staged-content guard.** `CommitSheet.swift:345` reads `guard phase == .editing, …`. After a hook rejection `phase` is `.failed`, so it falls straight through to `commit(mode:)` with no `stagedContentAtRisk` check — the second attempt silently discards `git add -p` work.

**4. `committedThenFailed` leaves Commit enabled.** Line 286 disables on `blockedReason != nil || phase == .committing`. The sheet says "Do not commit again" beside a live button that would.

Plus: `before` is captured outside the gate (`:1561` vs `:1566`), `committingTargets` is per-window where `creatingWorkrooms` is deliberately shared, suppression is keyed per row while the gate is keyed per project root, Cancel stays live during a commit and throws away the only report of the outcome, and a described-but-empty jj change can't be edited — the one state Describe exists for.

Also, an accident to disclose: `mktemp` was sandbox-denied, so a verification command's `cd` failed and the next line ran in the repo root, creating a stray "init" commit. I reset it — `HEAD` is back at `3095e338` and the tree is clean. Nothing of yours was touched.

content.content:
520	  /// Three things here are load-bearing, and all three were **measured** on git 2.x rather than
521	  /// reasoned about:
522	  ///
523	  /// 1. **A rename contributes BOTH sides.** `ChangedFile` carries `oldPath`, and the status layer
524	  ///    pairs renames (`.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so one row means two paths. Sending
525	  ///    only `path`: `mv old new` then committing `new` recorded an **add** and left `D old`
526	  ///    dangling in the worktree — staged, if the rename came from `git mv`. The user ticked one row
527	  ///    labelled `old → new` and got half a rename plus a mess.
528	  ///
529	  /// 2. **Every entry is `:(literal)`-prefixed.** `--` ends OPTION parsing, not MAGIC parsing, and
530	  ///    `--pathspec-file-nul` does NOT disable globbing either — its "taken literally" refers to the
531	  ///    absence of C-quoting in the file format, not to pathspec magic. Measured with `ab.txt` and
532	  ///    `a[b].txt` both modified: sending `a[b].txt` committed BOTH. A file named `*` would commit
533	  ///    the whole tree. `:(literal)` is what actually turns it off (verified: commits only the
534	  ///    bracketed file), and it still parses under `--pathspec-file-nul`.
535	  ///
536	  /// 3. **NUL separation, so no path needs escaping** — newlines and quotes in filenames pass
537	  ///    through unharmed, and thousands of long paths cannot blow the `E2BIG` argv ceiling at spawn,
538	  ///    where git would never get to emit anything classifiable.
539	  ///
540	  /// Order-preserving dedup: a rename whose `oldPath` is also its own `path` (or two rows naming the
541	  /// same file) must not send a duplicate.
542	  static func gitPathspecPayload(_ files: [ChangedFile]) -> Data {
543	    var seen = Set<String>()
544	    var out = Data()
545	    for file in files {
546	      for path in [file.path, file.oldPath].compactMap({ $0 }) where !path.isEmpty {
547	        guard seen.insert(path).inserted else { continue }
548	        out.append(contentsOf: Array(":(literal)\(path)".utf8))
549	        out.append(0)
550	      }
551	    }
552	    return out
553	  }

fix(macapp): close the nine defects the commit review found

The review of the commit write path landed four measured data-correctness
bugs and five structural ones. All nine, with the measurement each came
from:

- A plain `mv` rename failed the ENTIRE commit. libgit2 status runs with
  `.renamesWorkingTree`, so `mv old new` — what every editor and coding
  agent does; only `git mv` differs — arrives as one `.renamed` row whose
  new path git has never seen. Intent-to-add covered only `.untracked`
  rows, so `--only` refused with `pathspec … did not match any file(s)
  known to git` and committed nothing, taking every file ticked beside it
  down too. The intent-to-add payload also had to stop expanding renames
  to both sides: the old path no longer exists, and `git add` rejects a
  pathspec matching nothing.

- A successful commit could report "Committed, but something afterwards
  failed". The nothing-to-commit markers were matched against stdout
  before the exit-code guard, and git echoes the subject on stdout — so
  `-m "explain the nothing to commit error"` classified a clean exit-0
  commit as a failure, which the ref-moved check then upgraded. Now the
  guard runs first and jj's exit-zero no-op is matched on its own whole
  line, jj only.

- Retrying after a failure skipped the staged-content guard. It was
  conditioned on `phase == .editing`, so after a rejected hook the retry
  fell through unchecked and discarded anything staged with `git add -p`
  while fixing the rejection.

- `committedThenFailed` left Commit enabled beside copy saying "do not
  commit again". It is now its own terminal phase that disables both
  verbs.

- The before/after ref was read OUTSIDE the gate, so anything moving the
  ref while the call queued — a status snapshot, another window, the
  user's terminal during a 600s hook — could report a failed commit as
  one that landed.

- Commit suppression was per-window and keyed per row, where the gate is
  per process and per project root, and a worktree's index lives in the
  main repo. A second window kept probing a repo mid-write. It now lives
  on the shared ProjectStore, counted per project root.

- Cancel stayed live during a commit, tearing down the state its outcome
  is written into — a rejected hook after that was reported nowhere.

- A jj change that already HAD a description could not be opened, which
  is exactly "fix a typo in my message". The condition meant to allow an
  empty change was inverted.

- A failed commit left intent-to-add entries that break the user's own
  `git stash` until they reverse a change they never made.

Also: jj messages ride attached (`--message=`), since jj reads a detached
value beginning with `-` as another flag.

Merged and pushed. `331f3e03..9384b732`, no release cut.

**The review was not clean — nine defects, four of them data-correctness.** Fixed in `e1611e4c` before the merge.

The one that mattered most: **a plain `mv` rename failed the entire commit.** libgit2 status runs with `.renamesWorkingTree`, so `mv old new` — every editor, every coding agent; only `git mv` behaves differently — arrives as one `.renamed` row whose new path git has never seen. Intent-to-add covered only untracked rows, so `--only` refused with `pathspec … did not match any file(s) known to git` and committed **nothing**, taking every file ticked alongside it down too. My original integration test used `git mv`, which stages the rename, which is exactly why it passed while every real rename failed.

I proved the new test has teeth by reverting the fix — it failed with that error verbatim.

The other three: a successful commit could report *"Committed, but something afterwards failed"* (the nothing-to-commit markers were matched against stdout before the exit-code guard, and git echoes the subject there); retrying after a rejected hook skipped the staged-content guard entirely, discarding `git add -p` work; and `committedThenFailed` left Commit enabled next to copy saying "do not commit again".

Five structural: the before/after ref was read outside the gate, suppression was per-window and per-row where the gate is per-process and per-project-root, Cancel stayed live during a commit and threw away the outcome, a described jj change couldn't be reopened, and a failed commit left index entries that break the user's own `git stash`.

**Gates:** unit **1722/0** (was 1707, +15 regression tests), UI **10/10**, cargo **64/64**, lint clean.

Two things worth flagging:

- **A verification command damaged your repo and I reverted it.** `mktemp` was sandbox-denied, so a `cd` failed and the next line ran in the repo root, creating a stray "init" commit with two junk files. I reset to `3095e338` and confirmed a clean tree before continuing. Your git config was untouched. Everything after that ran in the scratchpad.
- **The five agents surfaced more than the nine.** Still open, none of them correctness: the dialog's file list is uncapped in a non-lazy `VStack` where `ChangesPanel` caps at 200; git Amend doesn't prefill HEAD's message, so it replaces the old one with whatever was typed for a new commit; the `sequencer` blocked-reason is computed but hardcoded `nil` at the only call site; and re-describing a jj change reformats a message with no blank-line separator. Worth a follow-up before Change 2.

content.text:
All four fixed, merged, pushed. `9384b732..17bc2388`, still no release.

**Render cap.** The list was an uncapped `ForEach` in a non-lazy `VStack`, where `ChangesPanel` — reading the same array — caps at 200. Since `summary`, `messageBody` and `excluded` are all `@State`, every keystroke rebuilt every row on the main thread. Now capped and lazy, and the truncation says so on screen. The risk a cap invites is a list that quietly disagrees with the commit, so the UI test asserts the button still claims all **257** files while only 200 are drawn. I also stopped `selectedCount` allocating a filtered copy of the change set six times per body pass.

**Amend target.** It replaced HEAD's message with whatever sat in a field that starts empty and normally holds a message written for a *new* commit — destroying text the user couldn't see. The commit is now named on screen (`a1b2c3d Add the session controller`), not just in a tooltip, since the repo's own rule is that nobody hovers to find out what a button will do.

**Sequencer.** The engine computed it and the dialog passed `nil`, so a parked merge was discovered by composing a whole message and pressing Commit. Resolved on appear, off the main actor, and passed to both verbs.

**jj round-trip.** `split` takes line 0 as summary and the rest as body; `message` rejoins with a blank line — so a stored description without that separator came back changed by someone who typed nothing. An unedited message is now recorded byte for byte. I verified that test has teeth by reverting the fix: it failed on `"line one\ntwo"` and `"subject\n\nbody"` exactly as it should.

One thing that fell out: preserving the original makes an untouched Describe a guaranteed no-op, which jj answers with `Nothing changed.` — a failure notice for changing nothing. That path now just closes.

**Gates:** unit **1727/0**, UI **13/13** (three new), lint clean.

Nothing else from the review is outstanding. Change 2 (Generate commit message) is the next real piece of work whenever you want it.
